title.zh: 卷一百二十四 載記第二十四 慕容寶 慕容盛 慕容熙 慕容雲
title.en: Volume 124 Records 24: Murong Bao; Murong Sheng; Murong Xi; Murong Yun
title.raw: 卷一百二十四 載記第二十四 慕容寶 慕容盛 慕容熙 慕容雲 Volume 124 Records 24: Murong Bao; Murong Sheng; Murong Xi; Murong Yun

sentences.zh: 慕容寶 慕容盛 慕容熙 慕容雲

translations.literal: Murong Bao; Murong Sheng; Murong Xi; Murong Yun
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao; Murong Sheng; Murong Xi; Murong Yun

sentences.zh: 慕容寶，字道祐，垂之第四子也。

translations.literal: Murong Bao, styled Daoyou, was the fourth son of Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao, whose courtesy name was Daoyou, was the fourth son of Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 少輕果無志操，好人佞己。

translations.literal: In youth he was frivolous and impulsive, without firm principles of conduct, and fond of having others flatter him.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was rash and unrestrained, lacking moral resolve, and delighted in those who flattered him.

sentences.zh: 苻堅時為太子洗馬、萬年令。

translations.literal: Under Fu Jian he served as Attendant to the Crown Prince's Horse and Magistrate of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: Under Fu Jian he held the posts of crown prince's attendant and magistrate of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 堅淮肥之役，以寶為陵江將軍。

translations.literal: In Fu Jian's campaign on the Huai and Fei, Bao was made General Who Crosses the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: During Fu Jian's campaign on the Huai and Fei rivers, Bao was appointed General Who Crosses the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 及為太子，砥礪自修，敦崇儒學，工談論，善屬文，曲事垂左右小臣，以求美譽。

translations.literal: When he became crown prince, he sharpened himself in self-cultivation, earnestly honored Confucian learning, was skilled at discourse and good at composition; he curried favor with the minor officials at Chui's side to seek a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: After he was named crown prince, he set himself to self-improvement, championed Confucian learning, excelled in debate and literary composition, and ingratiated himself with the lesser officials around Murong Chui in pursuit of a shining reputation.

sentences.zh: 垂之朝士翕然稱之，垂亦以為克保家業，甚賢之。

translations.literal: The court officials under Chui unanimously praised him, and Chui also thought he could preserve the family enterprise and greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chui's courtiers praised him in unison, and Chui himself believed he could safeguard the family's inheritance and held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 垂死，其年寶嗣偽位，大赦境內，改元為永康。

translations.literal: When Chui died, that same year Bao succeeded to the usurped throne, proclaimed a general amnesty within the realm, and changed the era name to Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: When Chui died that year, Bao took the throne, granted a general amnesty throughout the realm, and proclaimed the Yongkang era.

sentences.zh: 以其太尉庫辱官偉為太師、左光祿大夫，段崇為太保，其餘拜授各有差。

translations.literal: He appointed his Grand Commandant, the Kuru official Wei, as Grand Preceptor and Minister of the Left with the Splendor of Light rank; Duan Chong as Grand Tutor; the rest received appointments each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He made his grand commandant, the Kuru official Wei, grand preceptor and minister of the left with the Splendor of Light title; Duan Chong he made grand tutor; the remainder received promotions in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 遵垂遺令，校閱戶口，罷諸軍營分屬郡縣，定士族舊籍，明其官儀，而法峻政嚴，上下離德，百姓思亂者十室而九焉。

translations.literal: Following Chui's testamentary command, he reviewed household registers, abolished various military camps and subordinated them to commanderies and counties, fixed the old registers of the gentry families, and clarified their official protocol; yet the laws were harsh and government severe, superior and inferior were estranged in virtue, and among the common people those who thought of rebellion were nine out of ten households.
translations.idiomatic: He carried out Chui's dying instructions by auditing household registers, dissolving military camps and folding them into the civil counties, fixing the hereditary registers of the aristocratic clans, and clarifying official protocols—yet his laws were severe, his rule harsh, the court and the people grew apart, and in nine households out of ten the people were ready for revolt.

sentences.zh: 初，垂以寶塚嗣未建，每憂之。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Bao had not yet established an heir in the ancestral shrine, Chui worried about this constantly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Murong Chui had worried constantly because Bao had not yet named an heir.

sentences.zh: 寶庶子清河公會多材藝，有雄略，垂深奇之。

translations.literal: Bao's son by a concubine, the Duke of Qinghe, Hui, was talented in many arts and possessed bold strategy; Chui marveled at him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's son by a concubine, Hui, Duke of Qinghe, was gifted in many arts and possessed a bold strategic mind; Chui was deeply impressed by him.

sentences.zh: 及寶之北伐，使會代攝宮事，總錄、禮遇一同太子，所以見定旨也。

translations.literal: When Bao marched north to attack, he had Hui act in his stead in managing palace affairs; his overall supervision and ceremonial treatment were identical to those of the crown prince—this was how his intended appointment was made clear.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao marched north on campaign, he left Hui to manage palace affairs in his stead, with authority and ceremonial standing equal to the crown prince's—making plain that Hui was the intended successor.

sentences.zh: 垂之伐魏，以龍城舊都，宗廟所在，復使會鎮幽州，委以東北之重，高選僚屬以崇威望。

translations.literal: When Chui attacked Wei, because Longcheng was the old capital where the ancestral temple stood, he again sent Hui to garrison You Province, entrusting him with the weight of the northeast; he selected high-ranking subordinates to enhance his prestige.
translations.idiomatic: When Chui attacked Wei, he again stationed Hui at You Province to guard Longcheng, the old capital and seat of the ancestral temple, entrusting him with the defense of the northeast and appointing eminent subordinates to bolster his authority.

sentences.zh: 臨死顧命，以會為寶嗣，而寶寵愛少子濮陽公策，意不在會。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he gave a final charge that Hui should succeed Bao, but Bao doted on his younger son, the Duke of Puyang, Ce, and his heart was not set on Hui.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Chui charged that Hui should succeed Bao, but Bao favored his younger son Ce, Duke of Puyang, and had no intention of installing Hui.

sentences.zh: 寶庶長子長樂公盛自以同生年長，恥會先之，乃盛稱策宜為儲貳，而非毀會焉。

translations.literal: Bao's eldest son by a concubine, the Duke of Changle, Sheng, considering himself older as a son of the same mother, was ashamed that Hui should precede him; he therefore lavishly praised Ce as fit to be heir apparent while slandering Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's eldest son by a concubine, Sheng, Duke of Changle, resented that Hui, though born of the same mother, had been placed ahead of him; he loudly praised Ce as the rightful heir while denigrating Hui.

sentences.zh: 寶大悅，乃訪其趙王麟、高陽王隆，麟等咸希旨贊成之。

translations.literal: Bao was greatly pleased and thereupon consulted the Prince of Zhao, Lin, and the Prince of Gaoyang, Long; Lin and the others all spoke to please him and endorsed the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was delighted and consulted the Prince of Zhao, Lin, and the Prince of Gaoyang, Long; they all told him what he wished to hear and endorsed the plan.

sentences.zh: 寶遂與麟等定計，立策母段氏為皇后，策為皇太子，盛、會進爵為王。

translations.literal: Bao thereupon settled the plan with Lin and the others: he installed Ce's mother, the Duan clan, as empress, Ce as crown prince, and promoted Sheng and Hui to princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: Bao then settled the matter with Lin and the others: he made Ce's mother of the Duan clan empress, named Ce crown prince, and promoted Sheng and Hui to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 策字道符，年十一，美姿貌，而蠢弱不慧。

translations.literal: Ce, styled Daofu, was eleven years old, handsome in appearance, yet dull-witted and lacking intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: Ce, whose courtesy name was Daofu, was eleven years old, handsome in bearing, but slow-witted and lacking in intelligence.

sentences.zh: 魏伐并州，驃騎農逆戰，敗績，還于晉陽，司馬慕輿嵩閉門距之。

translations.literal: When Wei attacked Bing Province, the Flying Cavalry General Nong resisted in battle and was defeated; returning to Jinyang, the Marshal Murong Song shut the gates and barred him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei attacked Bing Province, the Flying Cavalry General Nong fought them and was defeated; on his return to Jinyang the marshal Murong Song shut the gates against him.

sentences.zh: 農率騎數千奔歸中山，行及潞川，為魏追軍所及，餘騎盡沒，單馬遁還。

translations.literal: Nong led several thousand horsemen in flight back to Zhongshan; when he reached the Lu River, Wei pursuit caught up with him, his remaining horsemen were all destroyed, and he escaped back alone on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: Nong fled with several thousand horsemen toward Zhongshan; at the Lu River Wei pursuers overtook him, his escort was wiped out, and he escaped alone on a single horse.

sentences.zh: 寶引群臣於東堂議之。

translations.literal: Bao led his ministers in council at the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Bao convened his ministers for counsel in the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 中山尹苻謨曰：「魏軍強盛，千里轉鬥，乘勝而來，勇氣兼倍，若逸騎平原，形勢彌盛，殆難為敵，宜度險距之。

translations.literal: The Governor of Zhongshan, Fu Mo, said: "The Wei army is powerful; fighting a thousand li from home, they come riding victory and their courage is doubled; if their swift cavalry range the plain, their momentum will grow still greater and they will be hard to match—we should take a defensible position and hold them off."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Mo, governor of Zhongshan, said: "The Wei army is formidable. Having marched a thousand li and riding the momentum of victory, their spirit is doubled. If their light cavalry sweep the open plain, their advantage will only grow—we should hold difficult ground and block them."

sentences.zh: 」中書令晆邃曰：「魏軍多騎，師行剽銳，馬上齎糧，不過旬日。

translations.literal: The Palace Secretary Qi Sui said: "The Wei army has many cavalry; their columns move with swift raiding speed, carrying grain on horseback—they cannot last more than ten days."
translations.idiomatic: The palace secretary Qi Sui said: "The Wei forces are mostly cavalry, marching in swift raiding columns with grain carried on horseback—they cannot sustain themselves for more than ten days."

sentences.zh: 宜令郡縣聚千家為一堡，深溝高壘，清野待之。

translations.literal: "We should order the commanderies and counties to gather households of a thousand each into one fort, dig deep moats and raise high ramparts, and clear the countryside to await them."
translations.idiomatic: "Let every commandery and county gather households into forts of a thousand families each, dig deep moats, raise high walls, and strip the countryside bare to wait them out."

sentences.zh: 至無所掠，資食無出，不過六旬，自然窮退。

translations.literal: "When they have nothing to plunder and no supplies to draw on, in no more than sixty days they will naturally withdraw in exhaustion."
translations.idiomatic: "Once they have nothing to loot and no supplies to draw on, within sixty days they will withdraw of their own accord, spent and starving."

sentences.zh: 」尚書封懿曰：「今魏師十萬，天下之勍敵也。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works Feng Yi said: "The Wei army now numbers a hundred thousand—the fiercest enemy in the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi, minister of works, said: "The Wei host now numbers a hundred thousand—the most formidable foe in the realm."

sentences.zh: 百姓雖欲營聚，不足自固，是則聚糧集兵以資強寇，且動眾心，示之以弱，阻關距戰，計之上也。

translations.literal: "Though the common people wish to gather in fortified settlements, they are not strong enough to defend themselves; this would only amass grain and troops to strengthen the enemy, stir popular alarm, show weakness, and block the passes to fight—that is the best plan."
translations.idiomatic: "Even if the people try to fortify themselves, they cannot hold out; we would only stockpile grain and troops for the enemy, unsettle the people, advertise weakness, and forfeit the advantage of blocking the passes in battle—that is the superior strategy."

sentences.zh: 」慕容麟曰：「魏今乘勝氣銳，其鋒不可當，宜自完守設備，待其弊而乘之。

translations.literal: Murong Lin said: "Wei now rides victory with keen spirit; their edge cannot be met—we should complete our defenses and wait for their exhaustion, then strike when they weaken."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Lin said: "Wei rides the tide of victory with keen morale; their edge cannot be met head-on. We should fortify our defenses and wait for them to weaken, then strike."

sentences.zh: 」於是修城積粟，為持久之備。

translations.literal: Thereupon they repaired the walls and stored grain, making preparations for a prolonged defense.
translations.idiomatic: They accordingly repaired the walls, stockpiled grain, and prepared for a long siege.

sentences.zh: 魏攻中山不克，進據博陵魯口，諸將望風奔退，郡縣悉降于魏，寶聞魏有內難，乃盡眾出距，步卒十二萬，騎三萬七千，次於曲陽柏肆。

translations.literal: Wei attacked Zhongshan without success, advanced and occupied Boling Lukou; the generals fled at the sight of them, commanderies and counties all surrendered to Wei; hearing that Wei had internal troubles, Bao led out his entire force to resist—120,000 foot soldiers and 37,000 cavalry—and encamped at Quyang Baixi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei failed to take Zhongshan and advanced to hold Boling Lukou; generals fled before them and commanderies and counties surrendered. Hearing that Wei was troubled within, Bao marched out his entire army—120,000 foot and 37,000 horse—and encamped at Quyang Baixi.

sentences.zh: 魏軍進至新梁。

translations.literal: The Wei army advanced to Xinliang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army advanced to Xinliang.

sentences.zh: 寶憚魏師之銳，乃遣征北隆夜襲魏軍，敗績而還。

translations.literal: Bao feared the keenness of the Wei army and sent the Northern Expedition commander Long to raid the Wei camp by night; he was defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Wei army's sharp edge, Bao sent Long on a night raid; Long was beaten and driven back.

sentences.zh: 魏軍方軌而至，對營相持，上下兇懼，三軍奪氣。

translations.literal: The Wei army came in close formation; the two camps faced each other. Superior and inferior were filled with dread, and the three armies lost their spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army arrived in tight formation and the two hosts faced each other across the lines. Dread spread through the ranks and the army's spirit collapsed.

sentences.zh: 農、麟勸寶還中山，乃引歸。

translations.literal: Nong and Lin urged Bao to return to Zhongshan, and he led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Nong and Lin urged Bao to withdraw to Zhongshan, and he turned back.

sentences.zh: 魏軍追擊之，寶、農等棄大軍，率騎二萬奔還。

translations.literal: The Wei army pursued; Bao, Nong, and the others abandoned the main force and fled back with twenty thousand cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Wei pursued. Bao, Nong, and the others abandoned the main army and fled back with twenty thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 時大風雪，凍死者相枕於道。

translations.literal: At that time a great wind and snow blew; those who froze to death lay piled along the road.
translations.idiomatic: A blizzard struck; the dead lay heaped along the road where men had frozen.

sentences.zh: 寶恐為魏軍所及，命去袍杖戎器，寸刃無返。

translations.literal: Bao feared being caught by the Wei army and ordered robes, staffs, and weapons cast away—not a blade was brought back.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing capture, Bao ordered robes, staffs, and weapons discarded—not a blade was carried home.

sentences.zh: 魏軍進攻中山，屯于芳林園。

translations.literal: The Wei army advanced to attack Zhongshan and encamped at Fanglin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army advanced on Zhongshan and encamped at Fanglin Garden.

sentences.zh: 其夜尚書慕容皓謀殺寶，立慕容麟。

translations.literal: That night the Minister of Works Murong Hao plotted to kill Bao and install Murong Lin.
translations.idiomatic: That night the minister Murong Hao plotted to kill Bao and install Murong Lin.

sentences.zh: 皓妻兄蘇泥告之，寶使慕容隆收皓，皓與同謀數十人斬關奔魏。

translations.literal: Hao's wife's brother Su Ni informed on them; Bao sent Murong Long to arrest Hao; Hao and several dozen fellow conspirators cut through the gate and fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's brother-in-law Su Ni betrayed the plot; Bao sent Murong Long to seize Hao, but Hao and several dozen conspirators broke through the gate and fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 麟懼不自安，以兵劫左衛將軍、北地王精，謀率禁旅弑寶。

translations.literal: Lin, in fear and unable to rest easy, took troops and seized the Left Guard General, the Prince of Beidi, Jing, plotting to lead the palace guard to assassinate Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, uneasy in his guilt, seized the left guard general, Prince of Beidi Jing, and plotted to lead the palace guard in assassinating Bao.

sentences.zh: 精以義距之，麟怒，殺精，出奔丁零。

translations.literal: Jing resisted on grounds of righteousness; Lin in anger killed Jing and fled to join the Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: Jing resisted on grounds of loyalty; Lin in fury killed him and fled to the Dingling.

sentences.zh: 初，寶聞魏之來伐也，使慕容會率幽、并之眾赴中山，麟既叛，寶恐其逆奪會軍，將遣兵迎之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Bao heard that Wei was coming to attack, he had sent Murong Hui to lead the forces of You and Bing to hurry to Zhongshan; after Lin rebelled, Bao feared Hui would seize the army in revolt and was about to send troops to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao first heard of Wei's invasion he had summoned Murong Hui with the armies of You and Bing. After Lin's rebellion he feared Hui would turn the host against him and prepared to send troops to receive him.

sentences.zh: 麟侍郎段平子自丁零奔還，說麟招集丁零，軍眾甚盛，謀襲會軍，東據龍城。

translations.literal: Lin's attendant Duan Pingzi fled back from the Dingling and reported that Lin was gathering Dingling forces, his troops were very numerous, and he planned to strike Hui's army and seize Longcheng in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's attendant Duan Pingzi fled back from the Dingling and reported that Lin was rallying Dingling warriors in great numbers, intending to strike Hui's army and seize Longcheng in the east.

sentences.zh: 寶與其太子策及農、隆等萬餘騎迎會於薊，以開封公慕容詳守中山。

translations.literal: Bao, with his crown prince Ce and Nong, Long, and more than ten thousand horsemen, went to meet Hui at Ji, leaving the Duke of Kaifeng, Murong Xiang, to hold Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao rode out with Ce, Nong, Long, and more than ten thousand horsemen to meet Hui at Ji, leaving Murong Xiang, Duke of Kaifeng, to defend Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 會傾身誘納，繕甲厲兵，步騎二萬，列陣而進，迎寶薊南。

translations.literal: Hui devoted himself to winning men over, repaired armor and sharpened weapons, and with twenty thousand foot and horse advanced in battle array south of Ji to receive Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Hui worked to win men's loyalty, repaired armor and sharpened weapons, and marched south of Ji with twenty thousand foot and horse in battle order to receive Bao.

sentences.zh: 寶分其兵給農，隆，遣西河公庫辱官驥率眾三千助守中山。

translations.literal: Bao divided his troops between Nong and Long and sent the Duke of Xihe, the Kuru official Ji, with three thousand men to help hold Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao divided his force between Nong and Long and sent Ji, Duke of Xihe, with three thousand men to reinforce Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 會以策為太子，有恨色。

translations.literal: Hui, seeing Ce made crown prince, showed resentment on his face.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui learned Ce had been named crown prince, resentment showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 寶以告農、隆，俱曰：「會一年少，專任方事，習驕所致，豈有他也。

translations.literal: Bao told Nong and Long; both said: "Hui is still young, entrusted alone with frontier affairs, and has grown proud through habit—surely there is no other cause."
translations.idiomatic: Bao told Nong and Long; both said: "Hui is young, entrusted alone with frontier command, and has grown proud through long habit—there is surely no deeper design."

sentences.zh: 臣當以禮責之。

translations.literal: "Your servant will reprove him with propriety."
translations.idiomatic: "We shall rebuke him as propriety requires."

sentences.zh: 」幽平之士皆懷會威德，不樂去之，咸請曰：「清河王天資神武，權略過人，臣等與之誓同生死，感王恩澤，皆勇氣自倍。

translations.literal: The gentlemen of You and Ping all cherished Hui's prestige and virtue and were unwilling to leave him; they all petitioned: "The Prince of Qinghe is gifted by Heaven with divine martial prowess and stratagems surpassing other men; we have sworn with him to live and die together, and moved by the King's grace our courage is redoubled."
translations.idiomatic: The men of You and Ping revered Hui and would not leave him; they petitioned: "The Prince of Qinghe is endowed with divine martial talent and stratagems beyond any other. We have sworn to live and die with him, and under your grace our courage is doubled."

sentences.zh: 願陛下與皇太子、諸王止駕薊宮，使王統臣等進解京師之圍，然後奉迎車駕。

translations.literal: "We beg Your Majesty and the crown prince and princes to halt at Ji Palace; let the King lead us to relieve the siege of the capital, and afterward we shall escort the imperial carriage."
translations.idiomatic: "We beg Your Majesty, the crown prince, and the princes to remain at Ji; let the prince lead us to lift the siege of the capital, and then we shall escort you home."

sentences.zh: 」寶左右皆害其勇略，譖而不許，眾咸有怨言。

translations.literal: Bao's attendants all feared Hui's courage and stratagem; they slandered him and permission was denied—the crowd all murmured in complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's attendants feared Hui's courage and stratagem, slandered him, and the request was denied; discontent spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 左右勸寶殺會，侍御史仇尼歸聞而告會曰：「左右密謀如是，主上將從之。

translations.literal: Attendants urged Bao to kill Hui; the attendant censor Chou Nigui heard and told Hui: "Those at your side are secretly plotting thus; the sovereign will follow them."
translations.idiomatic: Attendants urged Bao to kill Hui; the attendant censor Chou Nigui heard and warned Hui: "Those around the throne are plotting this in secret; the sovereign will heed them."

sentences.zh: 大王所恃唯父母也，父已異圖；

translations.literal: "What the Great King relies on is only his parents; his father already harbors other designs;"
translations.idiomatic: "All you rely on are your parents, and your father already plots against you;"

sentences.zh: 所杖者兵也，兵已去手，進退路窮，恐無自全之理。

translations.literal: "what he leans on is his troops, and the troops are already out of his hands; advance and retreat, road and refuge—he fears there is no way to preserve himself."
translations.idiomatic: "your troops are already slipping from your grasp. With neither advance nor retreat left, I fear you cannot save yourself."

sentences.zh: 盍誅二王，廢太子，大王自處東宮，兼領將相，以匡社稷。

translations.literal: "Why not kill the two kings, depose the crown prince, have the Great King install himself in the Eastern Palace, and concurrently hold the posts of general and minister to set the altars right?"
translations.idiomatic: "Why not kill the two princes, depose the crown prince, take the Eastern Palace for yourself, and hold both civil and military command to save the state?"

sentences.zh: 」會不從。

translations.literal: Hui did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Hui refused.

sentences.zh: 寶謂農、隆曰：「觀會為變，事當必然，宜早殺之。

translations.literal: Bao said to Nong and Long: "Seeing Hui's intent to rebel, the matter is certainly inevitable—we should kill him early."
translations.idiomatic: Bao told Nong and Long: "Hui means to rebel; it is inevitable. We should kill him at once."

sentences.zh: 不爾，恐成大禍。

translations.literal: "Otherwise I fear a great calamity."
translations.idiomatic: "Otherwise a great disaster will follow."

sentences.zh: 」農曰：「寇賊內侮，中州紛亂，會鎮撫舊都，安眾寧境，及京師有難，萬里星赴，威名之重，可以振服戎狄。

translations.literal: Nong said: "Bandits and enemies invade within; the central provinces are in turmoil; Hui pacifies the old capital, settles the masses and quiets the borders, and when the capital is in peril he comes a thousand li like a star—his prestige can awe the barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: Nong said: "Enemies press within and the heartland is in turmoil. Hui pacifies the old capital and keeps the borders quiet; when the capital is threatened he hurries a thousand li to the rescue. His prestige alone can overawe the barbarians."

sentences.zh: 又逆跡未彰，宜且隱忍。

translations.literal: "Moreover his rebellious traces are not yet manifest—we should for the time being endure in secret."
translations.idiomatic: "His treason is not yet open; we should endure a while longer."

sentences.zh: 今社稷之危若綴旒然，復內相誅戮，有損威望。

translations.literal: "Now the peril to the altars hangs by a thread; to kill one another within would harm our prestige."
translations.idiomatic: "The altars hang by a thread; fratricide now would only weaken us."

sentences.zh: 」寶曰：「會逆心已成，而王等仁慈，不欲去之，恐一旦釁發，必先害諸父，然後及吾。

translations.literal: Bao said: "Hui's rebellious heart is already formed, yet you, my kings, are benevolent and unwilling to remove him; I fear that once trouble breaks out he will first harm the princes, then reach me."
translations.idiomatic: Bao said: "Hui's rebellion is already formed, yet you are too merciful to act. Once he strikes, he will kill the princes first and then come for me."

sentences.zh: 事敗之後，當思朕言。

translations.literal: "After the affair fails, you will think of my words."
translations.idiomatic: "When disaster comes, remember what I told you."

sentences.zh: 」農等固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: Nong and the others firmly remonstrated, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Nong and the others remonstrated firmly, and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 會聞之彌懼，奔于廣都黃榆穀。

translations.literal: Hui heard and grew still more afraid; he fled to the Huangyu Valley of Guangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Hui heard and grew more afraid; he fled to the Huangyu Valley in Guangdu.

sentences.zh: 會遣仇尼歸等率壯士二千餘人分襲農、隆，隆是夜見殺，農中重創。

translations.literal: Hui sent Chou Nigui and others with more than two thousand stalwarts to attack Nong and Long separately; Long was killed that night, and Nong was gravely wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Hui sent Chou Nigui with more than two thousand men to strike Nong and Long; Long was killed that night and Nong gravely wounded.

sentences.zh: 既而會歸於寶，寶意在誅會，誘而安之，潛使左衛慕輿騰斬會，不能傷。

translations.literal: Presently Hui returned to Bao; Bao's intent was to kill Hui; he lured and reassured him while secretly sending the Left Guard Murong Teng to behead Hui—but could not wound him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then returned to Bao. Bao meant to kill him, lulled him with reassurances, and secretly sent Murong Teng of the left guard to strike him down—but Teng could not harm him.

sentences.zh: 會復奔其眾，於是勒兵攻寶。

translations.literal: Hui again fled to his troops; thereupon he marshaled his army to attack Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Hui fled again to his troops and marshaled them to attack Bao.

sentences.zh: 寶率數百騎馳如龍城，會率眾追之，遣使請誅左右佞臣，並求太子，寶弗許。

translations.literal: Bao fled with several hundred horsemen toward Longcheng; Hui led his host in pursuit and sent envoys demanding the execution of the flattering ministers at Bao's side and also asking for the crown prince; Bao refused.
translations.idiomatic: Bao fled with several hundred horsemen toward Longcheng. Hui pursued and sent envoys demanding the execution of Bao's flatterers and the surrender of the crown prince; Bao refused.

sentences.zh: 會圍龍城，侍御郎高雲夜率敢死士百餘人襲會，敗之，眾悉逃散，單馬奔還中山，乃逾圍而入，為慕容詳所殺。

translations.literal: Hui besieged Longcheng; the attendant Lang Gao Yun by night led more than a hundred dare-to-die men in a raid on Hui, defeated him, his host all scattered in flight, and he returned alone on a single horse to Zhongshan; he crossed the siege lines to enter and was killed by Murong Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Hui besieged Longcheng. That night the attendant Gao Yun led more than a hundred dare-to-die men against Hui, routed him, and his army scattered. Hui rode alone back to Zhongshan, slipped through the siege, entered the city, and was killed by Murong Xiang.

sentences.zh: 詳僭稱尊號，置百官，改年號。

translations.literal: Xiang usurped the honored title, established the hundred officials, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang seized the imperial title, appointed the full bureaucracy, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 荒酒奢淫，殺戮無度，誅其王公以下五百餘人，內外震局，莫敢忤視。

translations.literal: Dissolute in wine and extravagant in lust, killing without measure, he executed more than five hundred princes, dukes, and officials down to the lowest ranks; within and without trembled, none dared look him in the face.
translations.idiomatic: He drowned himself in wine and lust, slaughtered without measure, and executed more than five hundred princes, dukes, and officials; the court and the realm trembled, and none dared meet his gaze.

sentences.zh: 城中大饑，公卿餓死者數十人。

translations.literal: Famine gripped the city; several tens of the highest ministers starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the city and dozens of high ministers starved to death.

sentences.zh: 麟率丁零之眾入中山，斬詳及其親党三百餘人，復僭稱尊號。

translations.literal: Lin led the Dingling host into Zhongshan, beheaded Xiang and his intimate party of more than three hundred, and again usurped the honored title.
translations.idiomatic: Lin led the Dingling into Zhongshan, killed Xiang and more than three hundred of his kin and partisans, and again seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 中山饑甚，麟出據新市，與魏師戰於義台，麟軍敗績。

translations.literal: Zhongshan was in extreme famine; Lin went out to hold Xincheng and fought the Wei army at Yitai; Lin's army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan starved; Lin marched out to hold Xincheng and fought Wei at Yitai, where his army was routed.

sentences.zh: 魏師遂人中山，麟乃奔鄴。

translations.literal: The Wei army thereupon entered Zhongshan; Lin fled to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Wei entered Zhongshan; Lin fled to Ye.

sentences.zh: 慕容德遣侍郎李延勸寶南伐，寶大悅，慕容盛切諫，以為兵疲師老，魏新平中原，宜養兵觀釁，更俟他年。

translations.literal: Murong De sent the Attendant Li Yan to urge Bao to march south; Bao was greatly pleased; Murong Sheng remonstrated earnestly, holding that the troops were weary and the army aged, Wei had newly pacified the central plains, and they should nurture their forces and watch for openings, waiting for another year.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De sent the attendant Li Yan to urge a southern campaign; Bao was delighted. Murong Sheng remonstrated earnestly that the army was exhausted, Wei had only just pacified the central plains, and they should rest their forces, watch for weakness, and wait another year.

sentences.zh: 寶將從之。

translations.literal: Bao was about to follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was about to heed him.

sentences.zh: 撫軍慕輿騰進曰：「今眾旅已集，宜乘新定之機以成進取之功。

translations.literal: The Pacification General Murong Teng advanced and said: "The hosts are already gathered; we should seize this newly settled moment to accomplish the merit of advance."
translations.idiomatic: The pacification general Murong Teng urged: "The army is assembled; we should seize this moment of their fresh settlement to win a decisive victory."

sentences.zh: 人可使由之，而難與圖始，惟當獨決聖慮，不足廣采異同，以沮亂軍議也。

translations.literal: "Men may be led by you, but it is hard to plan the beginning with them; Your Sagely Consideration alone should decide—there is no need to gather many differing views and so disrupt the army's counsel."
translations.idiomatic: "Men can be led once the course is set, but they cannot help plan the start. Your Majesty alone must decide; do not canvass every dissenting voice and paralyze the council of war."

sentences.zh: 」寶曰：「吾計決矣，敢諫者斬！

translations.literal: Bao said: "My plan is settled—whoever dares remonstrate shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Bao said: "My mind is made up. Whoever dares object will be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 」寶發龍城，以慕輿騰為前軍大司馬，慕容農為中軍，寶為後軍，步騎三萬，次於乙連。

translations.literal: Bao set out from Longcheng; he made Murong Teng Grand Marshal of the vanguard, Murong Nong commander of the center, and himself commander of the rear—with thirty thousand foot and horse he encamped at Yilian.
translations.idiomatic: Bao marched from Longcheng, made Murong Teng grand marshal of the vanguard, Murong Nong commander of the center, and himself commander of the rear, and encamped at Yilian with thirty thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 長上段速骨、宋赤眉因眾軍之憚役也，殺司空、樂浪王宙，逼立高陽王崇。

translations.literal: The senior officer Duan Sugui and Song Chimei, because the host feared forced labor, killed the Minister of Works, the Prince of Lelang, Zhou, and compelled the installation of the Prince of Gaoyang, Chong.
translations.idiomatic: The senior officer Duan Sugui and Song Chimei, exploiting the army's fear of forced labor, killed Zhou, prince of Lelang and minister of works, and forced the Prince of Gaoyang, Chong, onto the throne.

sentences.zh: 寶單騎奔農，仍引軍討速骨。

translations.literal: Bao fled alone on horseback to Nong and still led the army to attack Sugui.
translations.idiomatic: Bao fled alone to Nong and still led troops against Sugui.

sentences.zh: 眾咸憚征幸亂，投杖奔之。

translations.literal: The host all feared the campaign and the disorder of fortune; they cast aside their weapons and fled to join the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers feared the campaign and the chaos of fate; they threw down their weapons and joined the rebels.

sentences.zh: 騰眾亦潰，寶、農馳還龍城。

translations.literal: Teng's host also collapsed; Bao and Nong galloped back to Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Teng's force collapsed as well; Bao and Nong galloped back to Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 蘭汗潛與速骨通謀，速骨進師攻城，農為蘭汗所譎，潛出赴賊，為速骨所殺。

translations.literal: Lan Han secretly conspired with Sugui; Sugui advanced to attack the city; Nong was deceived by Lan Han, stole out to join the enemy, and was killed by Sugui.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Han secretly allied with Sugui. Sugui advanced on the city; Nong was deceived by Lan Han, slipped out to join the enemy, and was killed by Sugui.

sentences.zh: 眾皆奔散，寶與慕容盛、慕輿騰等南奔。

translations.literal: The host all scattered in flight; Bao fled south with Murong Sheng, Murong Teng, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The army scattered; Bao fled south with Murong Sheng, Murong Teng, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 蘭汗奉太子策承制，遣使迎寶，及於薊城。

translations.literal: Lan Han supported the crown prince Ce to hold the government and sent envoys to welcome Bao; they met him at Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Han set Ce up as regent and sent envoys to welcome Bao, meeting him at Ji.

sentences.zh: 寶欲還北，盛等咸以汗之忠款虛實未明，今單馬而還，汗有貳志者，悔之無及。

translations.literal: Bao wished to return north; Sheng and the others all held that the sincerity of Han's loyalty was not yet clear—if he returned now alone on horseback, should Han harbor other intent, there would be no recalling the mistake.
translations.idiomatic: Bao wished to return north; Sheng and the others argued that Han's loyalty was still unproved—if he rode north alone and Han turned treacherous, it would be too late for regret.

sentences.zh: 寶從之，乃自薊而南。

translations.literal: Bao followed this and thereupon went south from Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Bao agreed and turned south from Ji.

sentences.zh: 至黎陽，聞慕容德稱制，懼而退。

translations.literal: When he reached Liyang he heard that Murong De had assumed power and, in fear, drew back.
translations.idiomatic: At Liyang he heard Murong De had taken power and drew back in alarm.

sentences.zh: 遣慕輿騰招集散兵于钜鹿，慕容盛結豪桀于冀州，段儀、段溫收部曲于內黃，眾皆響會，克期將集。

translations.literal: He sent Murong Teng to gather scattered troops at Julu; Murong Sheng rallied bold men in Ji Province; Duan Yi and Duan Wen gathered their followings at Neihuang—the host all responded and fixed a day to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Murong Teng to rally scattered troops at Julu; Murong Sheng gathered bold men in Ji Province; Duan Yi and Duan Wen mustered their bands at Neihuang; men answered from every side and a day was set to assemble.

sentences.zh: 會蘭汗遣左將軍蘇超迎寶，寶以汗垂之季舅，盛又汗之壻也，必謂忠款無貳，乃還至龍城。

translations.literal: When Lan Han sent the Left General Su Chao to welcome Bao, Bao, because Han was Chui's youngest brother-in-law and Sheng was also Han's son-in-law, was sure his loyalty was without duplicity and returned to Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Lan Han sent the left general Su Chao to welcome him, Bao—reasoning that Han was Chui's brother-in-law and Sheng his son-in-law—trusted his loyalty and returned to Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 汗引寶入于外邸，弑之，時年四十四，在位三年，即隆安三年也。

translations.literal: Han led Bao into the outer residence and assassinated him; he was forty-four years old, had reigned three years, in the third year of Longan.
translations.idiomatic: Han received Bao in the outer residence and assassinated him. He was forty-four, had reigned three years, in the third year of Longan.

sentences.zh: 汗又殺其太子策及王公卿士百餘人。

translations.literal: Han also killed the crown prince Ce and more than a hundred princes, dukes, and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Han also killed the crown prince Ce and more than a hundred princes, dukes, and ministers.

sentences.zh: 汗自稱大都督、大將軍、大單于、昌黎王。

translations.literal: Han styled himself Grand Commander, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and King of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Han styled himself grand commander, grand general, grand chanyu, and king of Changli.

sentences.zh: 盛僭位，偽諡寶惠湣皇帝，廟號烈宗。

translations.literal: Sheng usurped the throne and gave Bao the posthumous title of Emperor Hui Min and the temple name Lie Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng seized the throne and posthumously titled Bao Emperor Hui Min, with the temple name Lie Zong.

sentences.zh: 皝之遷于龍城也，植松為社主。

translations.literal: When Huang had moved to Longcheng, he planted pines as the lord of the soil altar.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Huang moved the capital to Longcheng, he planted pines as the spirit of the soil altar.

sentences.zh: 及秦滅燕，大風吹拔之。

translations.literal: When Qin destroyed Yan, a great wind uprooted them.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin destroyed Yan, a great wind uprooted the pines.

sentences.zh: 後數年，社處忽有桑二根生焉。

translations.literal: Several years later, at the site of the altar two mulberry roots suddenly sprang up.
translations.idiomatic: Years later, two mulberry shoots suddenly appeared at the altar site.

sentences.zh: 先是，遼川無桑，及廆通于晉，求種江南，平州桑悉由吳來。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liaochuan had no mulberry; when Wu opened relations with Jin he sought seed from south of the Yangtze, and all the mulberry of Ping Province came from Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Liaochuan had no mulberry; when Murong Wu opened relations with Jin he sought seedlings from the south, and all Ping Province's mulberry came from Wu.

sentences.zh: 廆終而垂以吳王中興，寶之將敗，大風又拔其一。

translations.literal: When Wu died Chui took the title King of Wu in restoration; when Bao was about to fall, the great wind again uprooted one of them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu died, Chui styled himself King of Wu in restoration; as Bao's fall approached, the great wind uprooted one of the mulberries again.

sentences.zh: 盛字道運，寶之庶長子也。

translations.literal: Sheng, styled Daoyun, was Bao's eldest son by a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, whose courtesy name was Daoyun, was Bao's eldest son by a concubine.

sentences.zh: 少沈敏，多謀略。

translations.literal: In youth he was deep and keen, with many stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was reserved and sharp, full of stratagems.

sentences.zh: 苻堅誅慕容氏，盛潛奔於沖。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian executed the Murong clan, Sheng fled in secret to Chong.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian slaughtered the Murong clan, Sheng fled secretly to Murong Chong.

sentences.zh: 及沖稱尊號，有自得之志，賞罰不均，政令不明。

translations.literal: When Chong assumed the honored title, he harbored self-satisfied ambition; rewards and punishments were uneven and government orders unclear.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong took the throne he grew self-satisfied; rewards and punishments were arbitrary and his orders unclear.

sentences.zh: 盛年十二，謂叔父柔曰：「今中山王智不先眾，才不出下，恩未施人，先自驕大，以盛觀之，鮮不覆敗。

translations.literal: Sheng, at twelve, said to his uncle Rou: "The Prince of Zhongshan now—his wisdom does not lead the host, his talent does not surpass those below him, his grace has not yet reached men, yet he is already proud and great; viewed by Sheng, few will not be overturned and ruined."
translations.idiomatic: At twelve Sheng told his uncle Rou: "The Prince of Zhongshan lacks the wisdom to lead and the talent to excel his followers; he has shown no grace to men yet already struts with pride. I see few who will not come to ruin."

sentences.zh: 」俄而沖為段木延所殺，盛隨慕容永東如長子，謂柔曰：「今崎嶇於鋒刃之間，在疑忌之際，愚則為人所猜，智則危甚巢幕，當如鴻鵠高飛，一舉萬里，不可坐待罟網也。

translations.literal: Before long Chong was killed by Duan Muyan; Sheng followed Murong Yong east to Changzi and said to Rou: "Now we are battered among blades, in a time of suspicion—if foolish we will be suspected by others, if wise we are as perilous as birds in a nest beneath a tent; we should be like the wild goose soaring high, rising ten thousand li in one flight—we cannot sit and wait for the net."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chong was killed by Duan Muyan. Sheng followed Murong Yong east to Changzi and told Rou: "We are battered among swords in an age of suspicion—play the fool and men will suspect you; play the wise and you are a bird in a burning nest. We must fly like wild geese ten thousand li at a stroke; we cannot wait for the net."

sentences.zh: 」於是與柔及弟會間行東歸於慕容垂。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Rou and his younger brother Hui he traveled east by secret ways to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: He and Rou and his younger brother Hui stole eastward to join Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 遇盜陝中，盛曰：「我六尺之軀，入水不溺，在火不焦，汝欲當吾鋒乎！

translations.literal: They met bandits in the passes of Shan; Sheng said: "My six-foot frame does not drown in water nor burn in fire—do you wish to meet my edge?"
translations.idiomatic: Bandits waylaid them in the Shan passes. Sheng cried: "This six-foot frame neither drowns nor burns—do you wish to test my blade?"

sentences.zh: 試豎爾手中箭百步，我若中之，宜慎爾命，如其不中，當束身相授。

translations.literal: "Try setting up your arrow in hand at a hundred paces—if I hit it, guard your life; if I miss, I shall bind myself and surrender."
translations.idiomatic: "Plant your arrow a hundred paces off. If I strike it, spare us; if I miss, I yield myself bound."

sentences.zh: 」盜用豎箭，盛一發中之。

translations.literal: The bandit set up the arrow; Sheng with one shot hit it.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit set the arrow; Sheng struck it with a single shot.

sentences.zh: 盜曰：「郎貴人之子，故相試耳。

translations.literal: The bandit said: "Young master, you are the son of a noble—therefore I tested you."
translations.idiomatic: The bandit said: "Young lord, you are a nobleman's son—I was only testing you."

sentences.zh: 」資而遣之。

translations.literal: He supplied them and sent them on.
translations.idiomatic: He gave them provisions and let them go.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，永誅俊、垂之子孫，男女無遺。

translations.literal: More than a year later Yong executed Jun and all of Chui's descendants, male and female, without exception.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Yong executed Jun and every descendant of Chui, male and female, without exception.

sentences.zh: 盛既至，垂問以西事，畫地成圖。

translations.literal: When Sheng arrived, Chui questioned him on western affairs and he drew a map on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng arrived, Chui questioned him about the west; he traced a map on the ground.

sentences.zh: 垂笑曰：「昔魏武撫明帝之首，遂乃侯之，祖之愛孫，有自來矣。

translations.literal: Chui laughed and said: "Formerly Wei Wu stroked Mingdi's head and thereafter enfeoffed him—the grandfather's love for his grandson has its own cause."
translations.idiomatic: Chui laughed: "When Cao Cao stroked Emperor Ming's head he later made him a marquis—a grandfather's love for his grandson runs deep."

sentences.zh: 」於是封長樂公。

translations.literal: Thereupon he enfeoffed him as Duke of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon enfeoffed him as Duke of Changle.

sentences.zh: 驍勇剛毅，有伯父全之風烈。

translations.literal: Valiant, brave, and resolute, he had his uncle Quan's fierce martial bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce, brave, and resolute, he bore his uncle Quan's martial spirit.

sentences.zh: 寶即偽位，進爵為王。

translations.literal: When Bao succeeded to the usurped throne, Sheng was promoted to princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao took the throne, Sheng was promoted to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 寶自龍城南伐，盛留統後事，及段速骨作亂，馳出迎衛。

translations.literal: When Bao marched south from Longcheng, Sheng remained to oversee rear affairs; when Duan Sugui rebelled, he galloped out to guard and receive him.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao marched south from Longcheng, Sheng stayed to manage affairs in the rear; when Duan Sugui rebelled, he galloped out to protect him.

sentences.zh: 寶幾為速骨所獲，賴盛以免。

translations.literal: Bao nearly fell into Sugui's hands and was spared only through Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bao nearly fell to Sugui and was saved only by Sheng.

sentences.zh: 盛屢進奇策於寶，寶不能從，是以屢敗。

translations.literal: Sheng repeatedly offered extraordinary stratagems to Bao, but Bao could not follow them, and therefore was repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng repeatedly offered bold stratagems to Bao, but Bao would not heed them, and so suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 寶既如龍城，盛留在後。

translations.literal: When Bao went to Longcheng, Sheng remained behind.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao went to Longcheng, Sheng remained in the rear.

sentences.zh: 寶為蘭汗所殺，盛馳進赴哀，將軍張真固諫以為不可，盛曰：「我今投命，告以哀窮。

translations.literal: When Bao was killed by Lan Han, Sheng galloped in haste to mourn; the general Zhang Zhengu firmly remonstrated that he should not, but Sheng said: "I now cast myself on their mercy and report my grief and destitution."
translations.idiomatic: When Lan Han killed Bao, Sheng hurried to mourn. General Zhang Zhengu urged him not to go, but Sheng said: "I go now to throw myself on their mercy and declare my grief."

sentences.zh: 汗性愚近，必顧念婚姻，不忍害我。

translations.literal: "Han by nature is foolish and narrow; he will surely think of the marriage bond and not bear to harm me."
translations.idiomatic: "Han is dull and shortsighted; he will remember our marriage and not harm me."

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，足展吾志。

translations.literal: "Within a month or so I shall have room enough to fulfill my purpose."
translations.idiomatic: "Within a month I shall have room to act."

sentences.zh: 」遂人赴喪。

translations.literal: Thereupon he entered to attend the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He went in to attend the funeral.

sentences.zh: 汗妻乙氏泣涕請盛，汗亦哀之，遣其子穆迎盛，舍之宮內，親敬如舊。

translations.literal: Han's wife, Lady Yi, wept and pleaded for Sheng; Han also pitied him, sent his son Mu to welcome Sheng, lodged him in the palace, and treated him with the same personal respect as before.
translations.idiomatic: Han's wife Lady Yi wept and pleaded for Sheng; Han pitied him too, sent his son Mu to welcome him, housed him in the palace, and treated him with the old intimacy.

sentences.zh: 汗兄提、弟難勸汗殺盛，汗不從。

translations.literal: Han's elder brother Ti and younger brother Nan urged Han to kill Sheng, but Han would not.
translations.idiomatic: Han's elder brother Ti and younger brother Nan urged him to kill Sheng; Han refused.

sentences.zh: 慕容奇，汗之外孫也，汗亦宥之。

translations.literal: Murong Qi, Han's grandson by a daughter, Han also spared.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Qi, Han's grandson by a daughter, Han spared as well.

sentences.zh: 奇入見盛，遂相與謀。

translations.literal: Qi entered to see Sheng, and they thereupon plotted together.
translations.idiomatic: Qi came to see Sheng and they plotted together.

sentences.zh: 盛遣奇起兵於外，眾至數千。

translations.literal: Sheng sent Qi to raise troops outside; the host reached several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng sent Qi to raise troops abroad; several thousand gathered.

sentences.zh: 汗遣蘭提討奇。

translations.literal: Han sent Lan Ti to attack Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent Lan Ti against Qi.

sentences.zh: 提驕很淫荒，事汗無禮，盛因間之於汗曰：「奇，小兒也，未能辦此，必內有應之者。

translations.literal: Ti was arrogant, cruel, and dissolute, serving Han without propriety; Sheng therefore slandered him to Han, saying: "Qi is a small boy and cannot manage this—there must be someone responding from within."
translations.idiomatic: Ti was arrogant, cruel, and dissolute and treated Han without respect; Sheng slandered him to Han: "Qi is a boy and cannot do this alone—someone inside must be helping him."

sentences.zh: 提素驕，不可委以大眾。

translations.literal: "Ti by nature is arrogant—he cannot be entrusted with a great host."
translations.idiomatic: "Ti is too arrogant to command a great army."

sentences.zh: 」汗因發怒，收提誅之，遣其撫軍仇尼慕率眾討奇。

translations.literal: Han in anger arrested and executed Ti and sent his Pacification General Chou Nimu to lead the host against Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Han in fury arrested and killed Ti and sent his pacification general Chou Nimu against Qi.

sentences.zh: 汗兄弟見提之誅，莫不危懼，皆阻兵背汗，襲敗慕軍。

translations.literal: Han's brothers, seeing Ti executed, were all in peril; they all raised troops against Han, attacked, and defeated Mu's army.
translations.idiomatic: Han's brothers, seeing Ti killed, feared for themselves, took arms against Han, and routed Mu's army.

sentences.zh: 汗大懼，遣其子穆率眾討之。

translations.literal: Han was greatly afraid and sent his son Mu to lead the host to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Han in great fear sent his son Mu to attack them.

sentences.zh: 穆謂汗曰：「慕容盛，我之仇也。

translations.literal: Mu said to Han: "Murong Sheng is my enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Mu told Han: "Murong Sheng is my enemy."

sentences.zh: 奇今起逆，盛必應之。

translations.literal: "Qi now rises in rebellion; Sheng is sure to respond to him."
translations.idiomatic: "Qi rebels now; Sheng will surely join him."

sentences.zh: 兼內有蕭牆之難，不宜養心腹之疾。

translations.literal: "Moreover there is trouble within the inner quarters—we should not nourish a disease of the heart and bowels."
translations.idiomatic: "With trouble in the inner court we should not harbor a disease at the heart."

sentences.zh: 」汗將誅盛，引見察之。

translations.literal: Han was about to execute Sheng and summoned him to observe him.
translations.idiomatic: Han was about to kill Sheng and summoned him to read his face.

sentences.zh: 盛妻以告，於是偽稱疾篤，不復出入，汗乃止。

translations.literal: Sheng's wife told him; thereupon he feigned grave illness and no longer went in or out, and Han stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's wife warned him; he feigned grave illness and did not leave his quarters, and Han desisted.

sentences.zh: 有李旱、衛雙、劉志、張豪、張真者，皆盛之舊昵，蘭穆引為腹心。

translations.literal: There were Li Han, Wei Shuang, Liu Zhi, Zhang Hao, and Zhang Zhen—all Sheng's old intimates whom Lan Mu had made his trusted inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han, Wei Shuang, Liu Zhi, Zhang Hao, and Zhang Zhen were Sheng's old intimates whom Lan Mu had drawn into his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 旱等屢入見盛，潛結大謀。

translations.literal: Han and the others repeatedly entered to see Sheng and secretly formed a great plot.
translations.idiomatic: They visited Sheng again and again and secretly formed a great conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 會穆討蘭難等斬之，大饗將士，汗、穆皆醉。

translations.literal: When Mu attacked and beheaded Lan Nan and the others, he held a great feast for the officers; Han and Mu both became drunk.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu attacked and killed Lan Nan, he feasted his officers; Han and Mu both drank deep.

sentences.zh: 盛夜因如廁，袒而逾牆，入於東宮，與李旱等誅穆，眾皆踴呼，進攻汗，斬之。

translations.literal: Sheng by night went as if to the privy, bared himself and climbed over the wall, entered the Eastern Palace, and with Li Han and the others killed Mu; the host all leapt and shouted, advanced to attack Han, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng slipped out at night as if to the privy, stripped, scaled the wall, entered the Eastern Palace, and with Li Han and the others killed Mu. The soldiers shouted; they attacked Han and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 汗二子魯公和、陳公楊分屯令支、白狼，遣李旱、張真襲誅之。

translations.literal: Han's two sons, the Duke of Lu He and the Duke of Chen Yang, were garrisoned separately at Lingzhi and Bailang; he sent Li Han and Zhang Zhen in raids to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Han's sons He, duke of Lu, and Yang, duke of Chen, held separate garrisons at Lingzhi and Bailang; Sheng sent Li Han and Zhang Zhen to kill them.

sentences.zh: 於是內外怗然，士女咸悅，盛謙揖自卑，不稱尊號。

translations.literal: Thereupon within and without were settled, gentlemen and ladies all rejoiced; Sheng with humble courtesy lowered himself and did not style the honored title.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without grew calm; men and women rejoiced. Sheng with humble courtesy declined the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 其年，以長樂王稱制，赦其境內，改元曰建平。

translations.literal: That year, styling himself Prince of Changle, he held the government, amnestied within the borders, and changed the era name to Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: That year he styled himself Prince of Changle, held the government, amnestied the realm, and proclaimed the Jianping era.

sentences.zh: 諸王降爵為公，文武各復舊位。

translations.literal: The princes were reduced in rank to dukes; civil and military officials all returned to their former posts.
translations.idiomatic: Princes were demoted to dukes; civil and military officers resumed their former posts.

sentences.zh: 初，慕容奇聚眾于建安，將討蘭汗，百姓翕然從之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Murong Qi had gathered troops at Jian'an intending to attack Lan Han; the common people all readily followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Murong Qi had gathered troops at Jian'an to attack Lan Han, and the people flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 汗遣兄子全討奇，奇擊滅之，進屯乙連。

translations.literal: Han sent his elder brother's son Quan to attack Qi; Qi struck and destroyed him, and advanced to encamp at Yilian.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent his nephew Quan against Qi; Qi destroyed him and advanced to encamp at Yilian.

sentences.zh: 盛既誅汗，命奇罷兵，奇遂與丁零嚴生、烏丸王龍之阻兵叛盛，引軍至橫溝，去龍城十里。

translations.literal: When Sheng had executed Han, he ordered Qi to disband his troops; Qi thereupon with the Dingling Yan Sheng and the Wuhuan king Long Zhi raised troops in rebellion against Sheng, led his army to Henggou ten li from Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Sheng killed Han he ordered Qi to disband; Qi instead joined the Dingling Yan Sheng and the Wuhuan king Long Zhi in rebellion, marching to Henggou ten li from Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 盛出兵擊敗之，執奇而還，斬龍、生等百餘人。

translations.literal: Sheng led troops out, defeated them, seized Qi and returned, and beheaded Long, Sheng, and more than a hundred others.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng marched out, defeated them, seized Qi, and beheaded Long, Sheng, and more than a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 盛於是僭即尊位，大赦殊死已下，追尊伯考獻莊太子全為獻莊皇帝，尊寶後段氏為皇太后，全妃丁氏為獻莊皇后，諡太子策為獻哀太子。

translations.literal: Sheng thereupon usurped the honored throne, proclaimed a general amnesty below the death penalty, posthumously honored his father's elder brother, the Crown Prince of Offered Splendor Quan, as Emperor Offered Splendor, honored Bao's consort of the Duan clan as Empress Dowager, Quan's consort Lady Ding as Empress Offered Splendor, and gave the crown prince Ce the posthumous title Offered Lament Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng then took the throne, granted amnesty short of death, posthumously honored his father's elder brother Quan as Emperor Offered Splendor, made Bao's consort of the Duan clan empress dowager, Quan's wife Lady Ding empress offered splendor, and gave Ce the posthumous title Offered Lament Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 盛幽州刺史慕容豪、尚書左僕射張通、昌黎尹張順謀叛，盛皆誅之。

translations.literal: Sheng's Governor of You Province Murong Hao, Left Vice Minister of Works Zhang Tong, and Governor of Changli Zhang Shun plotted rebellion; Sheng executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's governor of You Murong Hao, left vice minister Zhang Tong, and governor of Changli Zhang Shun plotted rebellion; Sheng executed them all.

sentences.zh: 改年為長樂。

translations.literal: He changed the era name to Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the era name to Changle.

sentences.zh: 有犯罪者，十日一自決之，無撾捶之罰，而獄情多實。

translations.literal: Criminals were judged by self-confession once every ten days; there was no punishment of flogging, yet the facts in the prisons were mostly true.
translations.idiomatic: Criminals confessed once every ten days; there was no flogging, yet cases in the prisons were largely truthful.

sentences.zh: 高句驪王安遣使貢方物，有雀素身綠首，集於端門，棲翔東園，二旬而去，改東園為白雀園。

translations.literal: The king of Koguryo sent envoys presenting local products; there was a sparrow, white in body and green in head, that gathered at the Gate of Correctness, perched and flew in the Eastern Garden for twenty days and then departed; the Eastern Garden was renamed White Sparrow Garden.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Koguryo sent tribute; a sparrow white-bodied and green-headed gathered at the main gate, dwelt in the Eastern Garden twenty days, then departed; the garden was renamed White Sparrow Garden.

sentences.zh: 盛聽詩歌及周公之事，顧謂群臣曰：「周公之輔成王，不能以至誠感上下，誅兄弟以杜流言，猶擅美于經傳，歌德於管弦。

translations.literal: Sheng listened to songs and to affairs of the Duke of Zhou; he turned to his ministers and said: "The Duke of Zhou's assisting King Cheng—he could not with utmost sincerity move superior and inferior, executed his brothers to stop slander, yet still monopolized beauty in the classics and sang virtue to pipes and strings."
translations.idiomatic: Listening to songs about the Duke of Zhou, Sheng told his ministers: "The Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng yet could not move court and people with perfect sincerity; he killed his brothers to silence rumor, yet still monopolized praise in the classics and songs."

sentences.zh: 至如我之太宰桓王，承百王之季，主在可奪之年，二寇窺窬，難過往日，臨朝輔政，群情緝穆，經略外敷，辟境千里，以禮讓維宗親，德刑制群後，敦睦雍熙，時無二論。

translations.literal: "As for my Grand Preceptor, Prince Huan, inheriting the end of a hundred kings, the sovereign was in years when the throne might be seized, two enemies peered in, hardship surpassing former days—yet facing court he assisted in government, popular sentiment was harmonious, outwardly he strategized and opened territory a thousand li, with ritual and deference he bound the clan, with virtue and punishment he controlled the host, kin were harmonious and serene, and in the age there was no second opinion."
translations.idiomatic: "My grand preceptor Prince Huan inherited an age when the throne could be seized, when two enemies watched and hardship surpassed any former day—yet he governed with harmony, opened territory a thousand li abroad, bound the clan with ritual, ruled the host with law and grace, and none disputed his rule."

sentences.zh: 勳道之茂，豈可與周公同日而言乎！

translations.literal: "Can such abundant merit of the Way be spoken of in the same day as the Duke of Zhou!"
translations.idiomatic: "Can such merit be named in the same breath as the Duke of Zhou's!"

sentences.zh: 而燕詠闕而不論，盛德掩而不述，非所謂也。

translations.literal: "Yet Yan's songs are omitted and not discussed, great virtue is covered and not recounted—is this what is called fitting?"
translations.idiomatic: "Yet Yan's songs pass in silence and his great virtue goes unrecorded—is that fitting?"

sentences.zh: 」乃命中書更為《燕頌》以述恪之功焉。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered the Palace Secretariat to compose anew the "Ode of Yan" to recount Ke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the palace secretariat to compose a new "Ode of Yan" recounting Ke's achievements.

sentences.zh: 又引中書令常忠、尚書陽璆、秘書監郎敷於東堂，問曰：「古來君子皆謂周公忠聖，豈不謬哉！

translations.literal: He also led the Palace Secretary Chang Zhong, Minister of Works Yang Qiu, and Secretariat Director Lang Fu into the Eastern Hall and asked: "The gentlemen of old all call the Duke of Zhou loyal and sagely—is this not mistaken!"
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the palace secretary Chang Zhong, minister Yang Qiu, and director Lang Fu to the Eastern Hall and asked: "Ancient gentlemen all call the Duke of Zhou loyal and sagely—is that not mistaken?"

sentences.zh: 」璆曰：「周公居攝政之重，而能達群臣之名，及流言之謗，致烈風以悟主，道契神靈，義光萬代，故累葉稱其高，後王無以奪其美。

translations.literal: Qiu said: "The Duke of Zhou bore the weight of regency and yet could make known the names of the host of ministers; when slander flowed he moved the fierce wind to awaken the sovereign—the Way matched the spirits, righteousness shone through ten thousand generations; therefore age after age they praise his height, and later kings have no means to deny his beauty."
translations.idiomatic: Qiu said: "The Duke bore regency yet revealed every minister's name; when slander rose he moved heaven's wind to awaken the king—the Way matched the spirits, righteousness shines through the ages, and no later king can deny his glory."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「常令以為何如？

translations.literal: Sheng said: "What does Director Chang think?"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng asked: "What does Director Chang think?"

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「昔武王疾篤，周公有請令之誠，流言之際，義感天地，楚撻伯禽以訓就王德。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "Formerly when King Wu was gravely ill, the Duke of Zhou had the sincerity of praying to yield his allotted years; in the season of flowing slander his righteousness moved Heaven and Earth; he whipped Prince Bo Qin to train and complete the king's virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said: "When King Wu lay gravely ill, the Duke prayed to yield his years; amid slander his righteousness moved heaven and earth; he whipped Bo Qin to complete the king's virtue."

sentences.zh: 周公為臣之忠，聖達之美，《詩》《書》已來未之有也。

translations.literal: "The Duke of Zhou's loyalty as minister and the beauty of his sagely penetration—since the Odes and Documents there has been none like him."
translations.idiomatic: "His loyalty as minister and sagely penetration—since the Odes and Documents none has matched him."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「異哉二君之言！

translations.literal: Sheng said: "Strange are the words of you two lords!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "Strange words, both of you!"

sentences.zh: 朕見周公之詐，未見其忠聖也。

translations.literal: "I see the Duke of Zhou's deceit and do not see his loyalty and sagacity."
translations.idiomatic: "I see the Duke of Zhou's deceit, not his loyalty and sagacity."

sentences.zh: 昔武王得九齡之夢，白文王，文王曰：「我百，爾九十，吾與爾三焉。

translations.literal: "Formerly King Wu obtained the dream of the nine-year span and told King Wen; King Wen said: 'I a hundred, you ninety; I give you three.'"
translations.idiomatic: "King Wu once dreamed the nine-year span and told King Wen; Wen said: 'I have a hundred years, you ninety; I give you three.'"

sentences.zh: 」及文王之終，已驗武王之壽矣。

translations.literal: "When King Wen ended, King Wu's lifespan had already been verified."
translations.idiomatic: "When Wen died, Wu's allotted span had already been fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 武王之算未盡而求代其死，是非詐乎！

translations.literal: "King Wu's allotted span was not yet exhausted yet he sought to die in another's place—is this not deceit!"
translations.idiomatic: "Wu had years left yet sought to die in another's stead—is that not deceit?"

sentences.zh: 若惑於天命，是不聖也。

translations.literal: "If deluded about Heaven's mandate, he was not sagely."
translations.idiomatic: "If he misunderstood heaven's mandate, he was not sagely."

sentences.zh: 據攝天位而丹誠不見，致兄弟之間有干戈之事。

translations.literal: Occupying and seizing Heaven's throne yet his red sincerity was not seen, he brought about armed strife between brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He seized heaven's throne yet showed no true loyalty, and set brother against brother in arms.

sentences.zh: 夫文王之化，自近及遠，故曰刑于寡妻，至於兄弟。

translations.literal: King Wen's transformation proceeded from what was near to what was far; therefore it is said he modeled punishment on his few wives, reaching to his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's teaching spread from near to far—'he modeled punishment on his wife, reaching even to his brothers.'

sentences.zh: 周公親違聖父之典而蹈嫌疑之蹤，戮罰同氣以逞私忿，何忠之有乎！

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou personally violated the sage father's canon and trod the tracks of suspicion, punished and killed those of the same breath to vent private resentment—where is the loyalty!
translations.idiomatic: The Duke violated his sage father's law, walked in suspicion, and killed kin to vent private wrath—where is the loyalty?

sentences.zh: 但時無直筆之史，後儒承其謬談故也。

translations.literal: But in the age there was no historian with a straight brush; later Confucians inherited their mistaken talk—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: But no historian wrote straight; later Confucians repeated the error—that is all.

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「啟金縢而返風，亦足以明其不詐。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "Opening the golden coffer and returning the wind is also enough to show he was not deceitful."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said: "Opening the golden coffer and stilling the wind proves he was not deceitful."

sentences.zh: 遭二叔流言之變，而能大義滅親，終安宗國，復子明辟，輔成大業，以致太平，制禮作樂，流慶無窮，亦不可謂非至德也。

translations.literal: Suffering the change of flowing slander from the Two Uncles, yet able to extinguish kinship in great righteousness, in the end secure the ancestral state, restore the son and clarify the throne, assist in accomplishing the great enterprise, arriving at great peace, establishing ritual and making music, flowing blessing without end—can this also be called not utmost virtue!
translations.idiomatic: Amid the Two Uncles' slander he could sacrifice kin for the state, secure the realm, restore the king, achieve peace, establish ritual and music, and bless posterity—can that be called less than utmost virtue?

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「卿徒因成文而未原大理，朕今相為論之。

translations.literal: Sheng said: "You, sir, only follow completed texts and have not traced the great principle; I shall now argue it with you."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "You only repeat finished texts and have not traced the great principle; I shall argue it with you now."

sentences.zh: 昔周自後稷積德累仁，至於文、武。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhou from Hou Ji accumulated virtue and benevolence, reaching to Wen and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou from Hou Ji onward accumulated virtue until Wen and Wu.

sentences.zh: 文、武以大聖應期，遂有天下。

translations.literal: Wen and Wu with great sagacity answered the age and thereupon possessed the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wen and Wu with great sagacity answered the age and won the realm.

sentences.zh: 生靈仰其德，四海歸其仁。

translations.literal: The living looked up to their virtue; within the four seas they returned to their benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: The people looked up to their virtue; the four seas returned to their benevolence.

sentences.zh: 成王雖幼統洪業，而卜世修長，加呂、召、毛、畢為之師傅。

translations.literal: Though King Cheng was young in inheriting the great enterprise, the allotted generations were long in repair; moreover Lu, Shao, Mao, and Bi were his teachers and tutors.
translations.idiomatic: Though Cheng was young when he inherited the throne, the dynasty's span was secure, and Lu, Shao, Mao, and Bi were his tutors.

sentences.zh: 若無周公攝政，王道足以成也。

translations.literal: Without the Duke of Zhou's regency, the kingly Way was sufficient to be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Without the Duke's regency the kingly Way would have sufficed.

sentences.zh: 周公無故以安危為己任，專臨朝之權，闕北面之禮。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou without cause took safety and peril as his own charge, monopolized the authority of facing court, and lacked the rites of facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Without cause the Duke made the realm's safety his own, monopolized court authority, and neglected the rites of facing north.

sentences.zh: 管、蔡忠存王室，以為周公代主非人臣之道，故言公將不利於孺子。

translations.literal: Guan and Cai loyally preserved the royal house, holding that the Duke's replacing the sovereign was not the Way of a minister; therefore they said the Duke would be unfavorable to the young lord.
translations.idiomatic: Guan and Cai loyally served the house and held that the Duke's replacing the king was no minister's way; they said the Duke would harm the young king.

sentences.zh: 周公當明大順之節，陳誠義以曉群疑，而乃阻兵都邑，擅行誅戮。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou ought to have made clear the integrity of great obedience, set forth sincerity and righteousness to awaken the host of doubts, yet he instead blocked troops in the capital, and on his own authority carried out executions and slayings.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke should have proclaimed great obedience and dispelled doubt with sincerity; instead he blocked the capital with troops and executed on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 不臣之罪彰于海內，方貽王《鴟鴞》之詩，歸非於主，是何謂乎！

translations.literal: The crime of disloyalty was manifest within the seas; he was about to present to the king the poem "Owl," returning blame to the sovereign—what is this called!
translations.idiomatic: His disloyalty was manifest throughout the realm; he would present the king the "Owl" poem and lay blame on his sovereign—what is that!

sentences.zh: 又周公舉事，稱告二公，二公足明周公之無罪而坐觀成王之疑，此則二公之心亦有猜于周公也。

translations.literal: Moreover when the Duke of Zhou undertook affairs he announced them to the Two Dukes; the Two Dukes were sufficient to clarify the Duke's innocence yet sat watching King Cheng's doubts—this shows the Two Dukes' hearts also harbored suspicion of the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke acted he reported to the Two Dukes, who could have cleared him yet watched Cheng's doubts—so the Two Dukes too suspected him.

sentences.zh: 但以疏不間親，故寄言于管、蔡，可謂忠不見於當時，仁不及于兄弟。

translations.literal: They only because the distant may not come between the near entrusted their words to Guan and Cai—loyalty was not seen in their time, benevolence did not reach their brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Because the distant may not divide the near they spoke through Guan and Cai—loyalty was unseen in their day, benevolence never reached their brothers.

sentences.zh: 知群望之有歸，天命之不在己，然後返政成王，以為忠耳。

translations.literal: Knowing that the host's hopes had a destination and Heaven's mandate was not on himself, only then did he return government to King Cheng—this was taken as loyalty, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the people's hopes lay elsewhere and heaven's mandate was not his, only then did he return power to Cheng—that alone was called loyalty.

sentences.zh: 大風拔木之征，乃皇天祐存周道，不忘文、武之德，是以赦周公之始愆，欲成周室之大美。

translations.literal: The omen of the great wind uprooting trees is that High Heaven blesses and preserves the Way of Zhou, not forgetting the virtue of Wen and Wu; therefore it pardons the Duke of Zhou's initial fault and wishes to accomplish the great beauty of the Zhou house.
translations.idiomatic: The great wind uprooting trees shows heaven blessing Zhou and remembering Wen and Wu's virtue—pardoning the Duke's first fault to perfect the house of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 考周公之心，原周公之行，乃天下之罪 人，何至德之謂也！

translations.literal: Examining the Duke of Zhou's heart and tracing the Duke of Zhou's conduct, he was a criminal under Heaven—how can this be called utmost virtue!
translations.idiomatic: Weigh the Duke's heart and trace his deeds—he was heaven's criminal; how call that utmost virtue!

sentences.zh: 周公復位，二公所以杜口不言其本心者，以明管、蔡之忠也。」

translations.literal: When the Duke of Zhou returned to power, the reason the Two Dukes sealed their mouths and did not speak their inmost hearts was to make clear Guan and Cai's loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke returned to power the Two Dukes kept silent to make clear Guan and Cai's loyalty."

sentences.zh: 又謂常忠曰：「伊尹、周公孰賢？

translations.literal: He also said to Chang Zhong: "Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—which is the more worthy?"
translations.idiomatic: He also asked Chang Zhong: "Which was worthier—Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou?"

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「伊尹非有周公之親而功濟一代，太甲亂德，放于桐宮，思愆改善，然後復之。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "Yi Yin did not have the Duke of Zhou's kinship yet his merit aided a generation; Tai Jia's virtue was disorderly and he was placed in the Tong Palace; reflecting on faults he improved, and thereafter was restored."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said: "Yi Yin lacked the Duke's kinship yet his merit saved a generation. Tai Jia's conduct was disorderly; Yi Yin placed him in the Tong Palace until he reformed, then restored him."

sentences.zh: 使主無怨言，臣無流謗，道存社稷，美溢來今，臣謂伊尹之勳有高周旦。

translations.literal: "He made the sovereign without complaint and the minister without flowing slander; the Way was preserved in the altars, beauty overflowed to this day—your servant holds Yi Yin's achievement higher than Zhou Dan's."
translations.idiomatic: "Sovereign and minister were at peace, the altars stood firm, and his glory endures—I hold Yi Yin's achievement above the Duke of Zhou's."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「伊尹以舊臣之重，顯阿衡之任，太甲嗣位，君道未洽，不能竭忠輔導。

translations.literal: Sheng said: "Yi Yin with the weight of an old minister held the eminent office of Chief Regulator; when Tai Jia succeeded to the throne the way of the sovereign was not yet harmonized, and he could not exhaust loyalty in assisting and guiding."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "Yi Yin as an old minister held the chief regency; when Tai Jia succeeded the kingly Way was unsettled, yet he failed to guide him with full loyalty."

sentences.zh: 而放黜桐宮，事同夷羿，何周公之可擬乎！

translations.literal: "Yet he deposed and placed him in the Tong Palace—the affair was the same as Yi of Xia—how can he be compared to the Duke of Zhou!"
translations.idiomatic: "He deposed him to the Tong Palace like Yi of Xia—how compare him to the Duke of Zhou!"

sentences.zh: 」郎敷曰：「伊尹處人臣之位，不能匡制其君，恐成、湯之道墜而莫就，是以居之桐宮，與小人從事，使知稼穡之艱難，然後返之天位，此其忠也。

translations.literal: Lang Fu said: "Yi Yin in the position of minister could not correct and control his sovereign, fearing that the Way of Cheng and Tang would fall and not be achieved; therefore he dwelt in the Tong Palace, associated with petty men, and made him know the hardship of farming—then returned him to Heaven's throne; this was his loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: Lang Fu said: "Yi Yin as minister could not correct his king, fearing Cheng and Tang's Way would fail; he kept Tai Jia in the Tong Palace among common men until he knew farming's hardship, then restored him—that was loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「伊尹能廢而立之，何不能輔之以至於善乎？

translations.literal: Sheng said: "If Yi Yin could depose and install him, why could he not assist him to reach goodness!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "If Yi Yin could depose and restore him, why could he not guide him to virtue!"

sentences.zh: 若太甲性同桀紂，則三載之間未應便成賢後，如其性本休明，義心易發，當務盡匡規之理以弼成君德，安有人臣幽主而據其位哉！

translations.literal: "If Tai Jia's nature were the same as Jie and Zhou's, then within three years he should not suddenly have become a worthy successor; if his nature was originally bright and excellent and his righteous heart easy to awaken, he should have done his utmost in the principle of correcting and guiding to assist in completing the sovereign's virtue—how can a minister seclude the sovereign and occupy his place!"
translations.idiomatic: "If Tai Jia were like Jie or Zhou, three years would not make a sage; if he were naturally bright, Yi Yin should have guided him without seizing the throne. How can a minister imprison his king and hold his seat!"

sentences.zh: 且臣之事君，惟力是視，奈何挾智藏仁以成君惡！

translations.literal: "Moreover a minister's serving his sovereign looks only to exerting strength—how can one embrace wisdom and hide benevolence to complete the sovereign's evil!"
translations.idiomatic: "A minister serves by giving all his strength—how can he hoard wisdom and hide benevolence to complete his king's ruin!"

sentences.zh: 夫太甲之事，朕已鑒之矣。

translations.literal: "As for the affair of Tai Jia, I have already taken it as a mirror."
translations.idiomatic: "I have already judged the affair of Tai Jia."

sentences.zh: 太甲，至賢之主也，以伊尹曆奉三朝，績無異稱，將失顯祖委授之功，故匿其日月之明，受伊尹之黜，所以濟其忠貞之美。

translations.literal: Tai Jia was a sovereign of utmost worthiness; because Yi Yin through three reigns had no different praise, he was about to lose the achievement of the illustrious ancestor's entrustment—therefore he concealed the brightness of sun and moon and accepted Yi Yin's deposition, thereby to complete the beauty of his loyal integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Jia was a most worthy king; Yi Yin served three reigns without equal praise and nearly wasted the founding kings' trust—so he accepted deposition to perfect the beauty of loyal integrity.

sentences.zh: 夫非常之人，然後能立非常之事，非常人之所見也，亦猶太伯之三讓，人無德而稱焉。

translations.literal: Only an extraordinary man can then establish an extraordinary affair—what an extraordinary man sees; it is also like Taibo's three yieldings, of whom men said there was no virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Only an extraordinary man can do an extraordinary thing—like Taibo's three yieldings, of whom the world said there was no virtue.

sentences.zh: 」敷曰：「太伯三以天下讓，至仲尼而後顯其至德。

translations.literal: Fu said: "Taibo thrice yielded the realm; only when Confucius came did his utmost virtue appear."
translations.idiomatic: Fu said: "Taibo thrice yielded the realm; only Confucius revealed his utmost virtue."

sentences.zh: 太甲受謗於天下，遭陛下乃申其美。

translations.literal: Tai Jia received slander from the realm; encountering Your Majesty he now has his beauty declared."
translations.idiomatic: Tai Jia was slandered throughout the realm; only now under Your Majesty is his virtue declared."

sentences.zh: 」因而談宴賦詩，賜金帛各有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon they conversed at a banquet, composed poems, and bestowed gold and silk each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: They feasted, composed poems, and bestowed gold and silk according to rank.

sentences.zh: 遼西太守李郎在郡十年，威制境內，盛疑之，累征不赴。

translations.literal: Li Lang, Governor of Liaoxi, had been in the commandery ten years and controlled the borders with authority; Sheng suspected him and repeatedly summoned him, but he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lang, governor of Liaoxi, had ruled ten years with iron control of the borders; Sheng suspected him and summoned him repeatedly, but he did not come.

sentences.zh: 以母在龍城，未敢顯叛，乃陰引魏軍，將為自安之計，因表請發兵以距寇。

translations.literal: Because his mother was in Longcheng he did not dare openly rebel; he secretly drew in the Wei army as a plan for his own security and therefore memorialized requesting to send troops to resist the invaders.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was in Longcheng, so he dared not rebel openly; he secretly courted Wei for safety and memorialized asking to send troops against invaders.

sentences.zh: 盛曰：「此必詐也。

translations.literal: Sheng said: "This is surely deceit."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "This is surely a ruse."

sentences.zh: 」召其使而詰之，果驗，盡滅其族，遣輔國將軍李旱率騎討之。

translations.literal: He summoned his envoy and interrogated him; it was verified as true, and he exterminated Lang's entire clan and sent the Pacification General Li Han with cavalry to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: He questioned the envoy and confirmed the plot; he exterminated Lang's clan and sent the pacification general Li Han with cavalry against him.

sentences.zh: 師次建安，召旱旋師。

translations.literal: When the army reached Jian'an, he recalled Han to turn the army back.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Jian'an, Sheng recalled Han.

sentences.zh: 朗聞其家被誅也，擁三千餘戶以自固。

translations.literal: When Lang heard his family had been executed, he gathered more than three thousand households to fortify himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing his family was executed, Lang gathered more than three thousand households to fortify himself.

sentences.zh: 及聞旱中路而還，謂有內變，不復為備，留其子養守令支，躬迎魏師于北平。

translations.literal: When he heard Han was returning midway, he thought there was internal trouble and no longer made preparations; he left his son Yang to hold Lingzhi and went in person to welcome the Wei army at Beiping.
