translations.idiomatic: Hearing Han was turning back, he thought there was internal strife, relaxed his guard, left his son Yang at Lingzhi, and went in person to welcome Wei at Beiping.

sentences.zh: 旱候知之，襲克令支，遣廣威孟廣平率騎追朗，及於無終，斬之。

translations.literal: Han, having learned of this, raided and took Lingzhi, sent the Broad Prestige Meng Guangping with cavalry to pursue Lang, caught him at Wuzhong, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Han learned of this, stormed Lingzhi, sent Meng Guangping with cavalry after Lang, caught him at Wuzhong, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 初，盛之追旱還也，群臣莫知其故。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sheng recalled Han, the ministers all did not know the reason.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng recalled Han, none of the ministers knew why.

sentences.zh: 旱既斬朗，盛謂群臣曰：「前以追旱還者，正為此耳。

translations.literal: After Han had beheaded Lang, Sheng said to the ministers: "Earlier I recalled Han for just this reason."
translations.idiomatic: After Han killed Lang, Sheng told the ministers: "I recalled Han for just this reason."

sentences.zh: 朗新為叛逆，必忌官威，一則鳩合同類，劫掠良善，二則亡竄山澤，未可卒平，故非意而還，以盈怠其志，卒然掩之，必克之理也。

translations.literal: "Lang had newly rebelled and was sure to fear official authority—on one hand he would gather his kind to plunder the good, on the other he would flee into mountains and marshes and could not quickly be pacified; therefore I returned contrary to expectation to fill and slacken his ambition, then suddenly cover him—it is the principle that he must be taken."
translations.idiomatic: "Lang had just rebelled and feared official power—he would either rally allies to plunder the innocent or flee into the hills. I recalled Han unexpectedly to lull him, then struck suddenly—that is how he had to fall."

sentences.zh: 」群臣皆曰：「非所及也。」

translations.literal: The ministers all said: "Beyond what we could reach."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all said: "Beyond our understanding."

sentences.zh: 李旱自遼西還，聞盛殺其將衛雙，懼，棄軍奔走。

translations.literal: Li Han, returning from Liaoxi, heard Sheng had killed his general Wei Shuang and, in fear, abandoned the army and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han, returning from Liaoxi, heard Sheng had killed his general Wei Shuang and fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 既而歸罪，復其爵位。

translations.literal: Presently he returned to acknowledge guilt and his rank and fief were restored.
translations.idiomatic: He later submitted and his rank and fief were restored.

sentences.zh: 盛謂侍中孫勍曰：「旱總三軍之任，荷專征之重，不能杖節死綏，無故逃亡，考之軍正，不赦之罪也。

translations.literal: Sheng said to the Attendant-in-Ordinary Sun Qin: "Han bore the charge of the three armies and the weight of independent command; he could not hold the staff and die in harness but fled without cause—in military law this is a crime that may not be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng told the attendant Sun Qin: "Han commanded the three armies with independent authority; he could not die at his post but fled without cause—in military law that is unpardonable."

sentences.zh: 然當先帝之避難，眾情離貳，骨肉忘其親，股肱失忠節，旱以刑餘之體，效力盡命，忠款之至，精貫白日。

translations.literal: "Yet when the Former Emperor was in flight and hardship, popular sentiment was divided and kin forgot their closeness, arms and legs lost loyal integrity—Han with a mutilated body exerted strength and exhausted his mandate, loyal sincerity reaching its utmost, essence penetrating the white sun."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet when the former emperor fled in hardship, kin forgot kin and ministers forgot loyalty—Han, though mutilated, gave his life with loyalty shining like the sun."

sentences.zh: 朕故錄其忘身之功，免其丘山之罪耳。」

translations.literal: "I therefore record his merit of forgetting his person and pardon his crime as great as a hill."
translations.idiomatic: "I record his merit of self-sacrifice and pardon his crime as great as a hill."

sentences.zh: 盛去皇帝之號，稱庶人大王。

translations.literal: Sheng removed the title of emperor and styled himself the Great King, a common man.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng laid aside the imperial title and styled himself Great King, a commoner in name.

sentences.zh: 魏襲幽州，執刺史盧溥而去。

translations.literal: Wei raided You Province and seized the governor Lu Pu and took him away.
translations.idiomatic: Wei raided You Province, seized Governor Lu Pu, and carried him off.

sentences.zh: 遣孟廣平援之，無及。

translations.literal: He sent Meng Guangping to aid him, but it was too late.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Meng Guangping to aid him, but too late.

sentences.zh: 盛率眾三萬伐高句驪，襲其新城、南蘇，皆克之，散其積聚，徙其五千餘戶於遼西。

translations.literal: Sheng led a host of thirty thousand to attack Koguryo, raided its Xincheng and Nansu, both took them, dispersed their stored grain, and moved more than five thousand households to Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng led thirty thousand against Koguryo, stormed Xincheng and Nansu, dispersed their stores, and moved more than five thousand households to Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 盛引見百遼於東堂，考詳器藝，超拔者十有二人。

translations.literal: Sheng led in audience a hundred men of Liao in the Eastern Hall, examined their talent and arts in detail, and elevated twelve of surpassing ability.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng received a hundred men of Liao in the Eastern Hall, examined their talents, and elevated twelve of outstanding ability.

sentences.zh: 命百司舉文武之士才堪佐世者各一人。

translations.literal: He ordered the hundred offices each to recommend one civil or military gentleman whose talent could aid the age.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every office to recommend one civil or military man fit to aid the age.

sentences.zh: 立其子遼西公定為太子，大赦殊死已下。

translations.literal: He installed his son, the Duke of Liaoxi Ding, as crown prince and proclaimed amnesty short of death.
translations.idiomatic: He named his son Ding, Duke of Liaoxi, crown prince and granted amnesty short of death.

sentences.zh: 宴其群臣於新昌殿，盛曰：「諸卿各言其志，朕將覽之。

translations.literal: He feasted his ministers in Xinchang Hall; Sheng said: "Each of you, my lords, speak your will—I shall review them."
translations.idiomatic: Feasting his ministers in Xinchang Hall, Sheng said: "Each of you speak your mind; I shall hear it."

sentences.zh: 」七兵尚書丁信年十五，盛之舅子也，進曰：「在上不驕，高而不危，臣之願也。

translations.literal: Ding Xin, Minister of the Seven Armies, fifteen years old and Sheng's nephew by a sister, advanced and said: "Not to be arrogant when above, high yet not in peril—this is your servant's wish."
translations.idiomatic: Ding Xin, minister of the seven armies, fifteen and Sheng's nephew, said: "Not to be arrogant when high, to stand tall yet not fall—that is my wish."

sentences.zh: 」盛笑曰：「丁尚書年少，安得長者之言乎！

translations.literal: Sheng laughed and said: "Minister Ding is young—how does he obtain an elder's words!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng laughed: "Minister Ding is young—how does he speak like an elder!"

sentences.zh: 」盛以威嚴馭下，驕暴少親，多所猜忌，故信言及之。

translations.literal: Sheng with stern authority controlled those below; the proud and violent had few intimates and he was much given to suspicion—therefore Xin's words reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng ruled with stern authority; the proud had few friends and he suspected much—hence Xin's words.

sentences.zh: 盛討庫莫奚，大虜獲而還。

translations.literal: Sheng attacked the Kumo Xi and returned with great captives.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng attacked the Kumo Xi and returned with great spoils.

sentences.zh: 左將軍慕容國與殿中將軍秦輿、段贊等謀率禁兵襲盛，事覺，誅之，死者五百餘人。

translations.literal: The Left General Murong Guo with the Palace Guard General Qin Yu, Duan Zan, and others plotted to lead the palace guard in a surprise attack on Sheng; the affair was discovered and they were executed—more than five hundred died.
translations.idiomatic: The left general Murong Guo with Qin Yu, Duan Zan, and others plotted to strike Sheng with the palace guard; the plot was discovered and more than five hundred were executed.

sentences.zh: 前將軍、思悔侯段璣、輿子興、贊子泰等，因眾心動搖，夜於禁中鼓躁大呼。

translations.literal: The Forward General, Marquis of Reflecting Repentance Duan Ji, Yu's son Xing, and Zan's son Tai, because popular sentiment was shaken, by night within the forbidden quarters beat drums, made a great clamor, and shouted.
translations.idiomatic: The forward general Duan Ji, Xing son of Yu, and Tai son of Zan, exploiting shaken morale, beat drums and shouted within the palace by night.

sentences.zh: 盛聞變，率左右出戰，眾皆披潰。

translations.literal: Sheng heard of the disturbance, led his attendants out to fight; the host all scattered and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng heard the uproar, led his guards out to fight; the mob scattered.

sentences.zh: 俄而有一賊從暗中擊傷盛，遂輦升前殿，申約禁衛，召叔父河間公熙屬以後事。

translations.literal: Before long one bandit struck and wounded Sheng from the dark; he was thereupon carried up to the front hall, renewed the covenant of the palace guard, and summoned his uncle, the Duke of Hejian Xi, to entrust the later affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an assassin struck Sheng from the dark; he was carried to the front hall, rallied the guard, and summoned his uncle Xi, Duke of Hejian, to entrust affairs.

sentences.zh: 熙未至而盛死，時年二十九，在位三年。

translations.literal: Before Xi arrived Sheng died; he was twenty-nine years old and had reigned three years.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had not yet arrived when Sheng died, aged twenty-nine, in the third year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 偽諡昭武皇帝，墓號興平陵，廟號中宗。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Emperor Zhaowu; his tomb was called Xingping Mausoleum and his temple name Zhong Zong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Emperor Zhaowu; his tomb was Xingping Mausoleum and his temple name Zhong Zong.

sentences.zh: 盛幼而羈賤流漂，長則遭家多難，夷險安危，備嘗之矣。

translations.literal: Sheng in youth was bound and cast adrift in hardship; grown, he encountered many family calamities; ease and peril, safety and danger, he tasted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng in youth knew bondage and exile; grown, he endured endless family calamity—ease and peril, safety and danger, he tasted them all.

sentences.zh: 懲寶暗而不斷，遂峻機威刑，織芥之嫌，莫不裁之於未萌，防之於未兆。

translations.literal: Chastising Bao's darkness and inability to decide, he thereupon made severe his authority and punishments; resentments fine as a fiber, none were not cut off in the ungrown bud and guarded against in the unmanifest omen.
translations.idiomatic: Chastising Bao's blindness and indecision, he sharpened authority and punishment; the slightest grudge was cut off before it sprouted.

sentences.zh: 於是上下振局，人不自安，雖忠誠親戚亦皆離貳，舊臣靡不夷滅，安忍無親，所以卒於不免。

translations.literal: Thereupon superior and inferior trembled, men did not feel secure in themselves; even loyal kinsmen by marriage all turned away, old ministers none were not destroyed—cruel and without kin—and therefore in the end he could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Court and people trembled; even loyal kin turned away and old ministers were destroyed—cruel and kinless—and so he could not escape his end.

sentences.zh: 是歲隆安五年也。

translations.literal: This was the fifth year of Longan.
translations.idiomatic: This was the fifth year of Longan.

sentences.zh: 熙字道文，垂之少子也。

translations.literal: Xi, styled Daowen, was Chui's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, whose courtesy name was Daowen, was Chui's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 初封河間王。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 段速骨之難，諸王多被其害，熙素為高陽王崇所親愛，故得免焉。

translations.literal: In the hardship of Duan Sugui, many princes suffered harm; Xi by nature was loved and cherished by the Prince of Gaoyang Chong, and therefore escaped.
translations.idiomatic: In Duan Sugui's rebellion many princes perished; Xi was beloved by Prince of Gaoyang Chong and so escaped.

sentences.zh: 蘭汗之篡也，以熙為遼東公，備宗祀之義。

translations.literal: When Lan Han usurped, he made Xi Duke of Liaodong to supply the meaning of ancestral sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When Lan Han usurped, he made Xi Duke of Liaodong to maintain the ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 盛初即位，降爵為公，拜都督中外諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射，領中領軍。

translations.literal: When Sheng first assumed the throne, Xi was reduced in rank to duke and appointed Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, Flying Cavalry Grand General, and Left Vice Minister of Works, holding the office of Central Commander of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng first took the throne, Xi was demoted to duke and made commander-in-chief of all armies, flying cavalry grand general, left vice minister of works, and central commander of the guard.

sentences.zh: 從征高句驪、契丹，皆勇冠諸將。

translations.literal: Following campaigns against Koguryo and the Khitan, in courage he led all the generals.
translations.idiomatic: On campaigns against Koguryo and the Khitan his courage led every general.

sentences.zh: 盛曰：「叔父雄果英壯，有世祖之風，但弘略不如耳。」

translations.literal: Sheng said: "Uncle is heroic, resolute, and stalwart, with the wind of Shizu—but his broad strategy is not equal."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "Uncle is heroic and stalwart, with Shizu's spirit—but his broad strategy falls short."

sentences.zh: 及盛死，其太后丁氏以國多難，宜立長君。

translations.literal: When Sheng died, his Empress Dowager Ding, because the state had many hardships, held that a mature sovereign should be established.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng died, Empress Dowager Ding, because the state was in turmoil, held that a mature ruler should be installed.

sentences.zh: 群望皆在平原西元，而丁氏意在於熙，遂廢太子定，迎熙入宮。

translations.literal: The host's hopes were all on Pingyuan Xi Yuan, but Lady Ding's heart was set on Xi; they thereupon deposed the crown prince Ding and welcomed Xi into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Popular hope rested on Yuan of Pingyuan, but Lady Ding favored Xi; they deposed Crown Prince Ding and welcomed Xi to the palace.

sentences.zh: 群臣勸進，熙以讓元，元固以讓熙，熙遂僭即尊位。

translations.literal: The ministers urged him to advance; Xi yielded to Yuan, Yuan firmly yielded to Xi, and Xi thereupon usurped the honored throne.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers urged him forward; Xi yielded to Yuan, Yuan firmly yielded to Xi, and Xi took the throne.

sentences.zh: 誅其大臣段璣、秦興等，並夷三族。

translations.literal: He executed his great ministers Duan Ji, Qin Xing, and the others, and exterminated their three clans.
translations.idiomatic: He executed the great ministers Duan Ji, Qin Xing, and others and exterminated their three clans.

sentences.zh: 元以嫌疑賜死。

translations.literal: Yuan was given death because of suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was forced to die on suspicion.

sentences.zh: 元字道光，寶之第四子也。

translations.literal: Yuan, styled Daoguang, was Bao's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, whose courtesy name was Daoguang, was Bao's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 赦殊死已下，改元曰光始，改北燕台為大單于台，置左右輔，位次尚書。

translations.literal: He amnestied short of death, changed the era name to Guangshi, changed the Northern Yan Terrace to the Grand Chanyu Terrace, and established Left and Right Assistants, ranking below the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He granted amnesty short of death, proclaimed the Guangshi era, renamed the Northern Yan Terrace the Grand Chanyu Terrace, and established left and right assistants ranking below the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 初，熙烝于丁氏，故為所立。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xi had violated propriety with Lady Ding, and therefore was installed by her.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xi had violated propriety with Lady Ding, and therefore she installed him.

sentences.zh: 及寵倖苻貴人，丁氏怨恚呪詛，與兄子七兵尚書信謀廢熙。

translations.literal: When he favored the Honored Lady of the Fu clan, Lady Ding in resentment and rage cursed, and with her elder brother's son, Minister of the Seven Armies Xin, plotted to depose Xi.
translations.idiomatic: When he favored Lady Fu, Lady Ding cursed in rage and with her nephew Ding Xin plotted to depose Xi.

sentences.zh: 熙聞之，大怒，逼丁氏令自殺，葬以後禮，誅丁信。

translations.literal: Xi heard of it, was greatly angry, compelled Lady Ding to kill herself, buried her with the rites due a consort, and executed Ding Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Xi in fury forced Lady Ding to kill herself, buried her with consort's rites, and executed Ding Xin.

sentences.zh: 熙狩于北原，石城令高和殺司隸校尉張顯，閉門距熙。

translations.literal: Xi hunted on the Northern Plain; the Magistrate of Shicheng Gao He killed the Director of the Masters of Writing Zhang Xian, shut the gates, and barred Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi hunted on the northern plain; the magistrate of Shicheng Gao He killed the director Zhang Xian, shut the gates, and barred Xi.

sentences.zh: 熙率騎馳返，和眾皆投杖，熙入誅之。

translations.literal: Xi led cavalry in galloping return; He and the host all cast aside their staffs; Xi entered and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi galloped back; He and his men threw down their weapons; Xi entered and killed him.

sentences.zh: 於是引見州郡及單于八部耆舊於東宮，問以疾苦。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led in audience the governors of provinces and commanderies and the elders of the eight tribes of the Chanyu in the Eastern Palace and asked them about their hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He then received governors and the eight tribal elders of the chanyu in the Eastern Palace and asked after their hardships.

sentences.zh: 大築龍騰苑，廣袤十餘里，役徒二萬人。

translations.literal: He greatly built Longteng Garden, more than ten li in breadth; corvée laborers numbered twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He built Longteng Garden, more than ten li across, with twenty thousand corvée laborers.

sentences.zh: 起景雲山于苑內，基廣五百步，峰高十七丈。

translations.literal: He raised Jingyun Mountain within the garden, its base five hundred paces broad and its peak seventeen zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: Within the garden he raised Jingyun Mountain, five hundred paces at the base and seventeen zhang high.

sentences.zh: 又起逍遙宮、甘露殿，連房數百，觀閣相交。

translations.literal: He also raised Xiaoyao Palace and Ganlu Hall, linked chambers in the hundreds, towers and pavilions intersecting.
translations.idiomatic: He also built Xiaoyao Palace and Ganlu Hall—hundreds of linked chambers with towers and pavilions intertwined.

sentences.zh: 鑿天河渠，引水入宮。

translations.literal: He dug the Tianhe Canal to draw water into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He dug the Tianhe Canal to bring water into the palace.

sentences.zh: 又為其昭儀苻氏鑿曲光海、清涼池。

translations.literal: He also for his Lady of Bright Composure of the Fu clan dug Quguang Sea and Qingliang Pool.
translations.idiomatic: For his lady of bright composure, Lady Fu, he dug Quguang Sea and Qingliang Pool.

sentences.zh: 季夏盛暑，士卒不得休息，暍死者太半。

translations.literal: In the height of summer's heat the soldiers could not rest; more than half died of heat.
translations.idiomatic: In midsummer heat the laborers could not rest; more than half died of sunstroke.

sentences.zh: 熙游于城南，止大柳樹下，若有人呼曰：「大王且止。

translations.literal: Xi toured south of the city and stopped beneath a great willow tree; it was as if someone called: "Great King, halt for a moment."
translations.idiomatic: Xi toured south of the city and stopped under a great willow; someone seemed to call: "Great King, halt."

sentences.zh: 」熙惡之，伐其樹，乃有蛇長丈餘，從樹中而出。

translations.literal: Xi hated this, felled the tree, and thereupon a serpent more than a zhang long came out from within the tree.
translations.idiomatic: Xi in disgust felled the tree, and a serpent more than a zhang long emerged from within.

sentences.zh: 立其貴嬪苻氏為皇后，赦殊死已下。

translations.literal: He installed his Honored Consort of the Fu clan as empress and amnestied short of death.
translations.idiomatic: He made his honored consort Lady Fu empress and granted amnesty short of death.

sentences.zh: 熙北襲契丹，大破之。

translations.literal: Xi raided the Khitan in the north and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Xi raided the Khitan in the north and routed them.

sentences.zh: 昭儀苻氏死，偽諡湣皇后。

translations.literal: The Lady of Bright Composure of the Fu clan died; her posthumous title was Empress Min.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fu of bright composure died; she was posthumously titled Empress Min.

sentences.zh: 贈苻謨太宰，諡文獻公。

translations.literal: He gave Fu Mo the post of Grand Preceptor and the posthumous title Duke of Literature and Offered.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Fu Mo the post of grand preceptor and the posthumous title Duke of Literature and Offered.

sentences.zh: 二苻並美而豔，好微行遊宴，熙弗之禁也。

translations.literal: Both ladies of the Fu clan were beautiful and alluring, fond of going out in disguise on tours and feasts; Xi did not forbid them.
translations.idiomatic: Both Fu ladies were beautiful and fond of disguised outings and feasts; Xi did not forbid them.

sentences.zh: 請謁必從，刑賞大政無不由之。

translations.literal: When they requested audiences he always followed; great punishments and rewards and major government—none did not proceed from them.
translations.idiomatic: He always accompanied their audiences; punishments, rewards, and major policy all proceeded from them.

sentences.zh: 初，昭儀有疾，龍城人王溫稱能療之，未幾而卒，熙忿其妄也，立於公車門支解溫而焚之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Lady of Bright Composure was ill, a man of Longcheng, Wang Wen, claimed he could cure her; before long she died; Xi in anger at his falsehood stood him at the public carriage gate, dismembered Wen, and burned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Fu fell ill, Wang Wen of Longcheng claimed he could cure her; she soon died. Xi in rage had Wen dismembered at the public gate and burned.

sentences.zh: 其後好游田，熙從之，北登白鹿山，東過青嶺，南臨滄海，百姓苦之，士卒為豺狼所害及凍死者五千餘人矣。

translations.literal: Afterward he was fond of roaming the hunt fields; Xi followed him, ascending north to Bailu Mountain, passing east over Qing Ridge, facing south over the blue sea—the common people suffered bitterly; soldiers killed by wolves and those who froze to death were more than five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He then loved the hunt; Xi followed him north to Bailu Mountain, east over Qing Ridge, south to the sea—the people suffered; more than five thousand soldiers died of wolves or frost.

sentences.zh: 會高句驪寇燕郡，殺略百餘人。

translations.literal: When Koguryo raided Yan Commandery and killed and plundered more than a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Koguryo raided Yan Commandery and killed and plundered more than a hundred people.

sentences.zh: 熙伐高句驪，以苻氏從，為沖車地道以攻遼東。

translations.literal: Xi attacked Koguryo; the Fu clan followed; he made battering rams and underground passages to attack Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Xi attacked Koguryo with Lady Fu in train, building rams and tunnels against Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 熙曰：「待剗平寇城，朕當與後乘輦而入，不聽將士先登。

translations.literal: Xi said: "Wait until we level the bandit city— I shall enter in the rear carriage with the consort; I do not listen to the officers and soldiers climbing first."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said: "When the rebel city is leveled I shall enter in the rear carriage with the empress; I forbid the soldiers to climb first."

sentences.zh: 」於是城內嚴備，攻之不能下。

translations.literal: Thereupon within the city they made strict preparations and attacked but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The city made strict preparations and the attack failed.

sentences.zh: 會大雨雪，士卒多死，乃引歸。

translations.literal: When great rain and snow came, many soldiers died; he thereupon led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rain and snow killed many soldiers; he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 擬鄴之鳳陽門，作弘光門，累級三層。

translations.literal: Patterning himself on Ye's Fengyang Gate, he made the Hongguang Gate with three tiers of steps.
translations.idiomatic: Modeling Ye's Fengyang Gate, he built the Hongguang Gate with three tiers of steps.

sentences.zh: 熙與苻氏襲契丹，憚其眾盛，將還，苻氏弗聽，遂棄輜重，輕襲高句驪，周行三千餘里，士馬疲凍，死者屬路。

translations.literal: Xi with the Fu clan raided the Khitan; fearing their great numbers, he was about to return, but the Fu clan would not listen; he thereupon abandoned baggage and supplies and made a light raid on Koguryo, circling more than three thousand li; men and horses were weary and frozen, the dead lining the road.
translations.idiomatic: Xi raided the Khitan with Lady Fu; fearing their numbers he turned back, but she refused. He abandoned baggage for a light strike on Koguryo, marching three thousand li; men and horses froze and the dead lined the road.

sentences.zh: 攻木底城，不克而還。

translations.literal: He attacked Mudi city, could not take it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Mudi city, failed, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 盡殺寶諸子。

translations.literal: He executed all of Bao's sons.
translations.idiomatic: He executed all of Bao's sons.

sentences.zh: 大城肥如及宿軍，以仇尼倪為鎮東大將軍、營州刺史，鎮宿軍，上庸公懿為鎮西將軍、幽州刺史，鎮令支；

translations.literal: He fortified Feiru in Dacheng and Sujun, made Chou Nini Pacification General of the East and Governor of Ying Province to garrison Sujun, and the Duke of Shangyong Yi Pacification General of the West and Governor of You to garrison Lingzhi;
translations.idiomatic: He fortified Feiru in Dacheng and Sujun, made Chou Nini pacification general of the east and governor of Ying to garrison Sujun, and Yi, duke of Shangyong, pacification general of the west and governor of You to garrison Lingzhi;

sentences.zh: 尚書劉木為鎮南大將軍、冀州刺史，鎮肥如。

translations.literal: the Minister of Works Liu Mu was made Pacification General of the South and Governor of Ji to garrison Feiru.
translations.idiomatic: and Liu Mu, minister of works, pacification general of the south and governor of Ji to garrison Feiru.

sentences.zh: 為苻氏起承華殿，高承光一倍，負土於北門，土與穀同價。

translations.literal: For the Fu clan he raised Chenghua Hall, twice the height of Chengguang; they carried earth at the northern gate, and earth was the same price as grain.
translations.idiomatic: For Lady Fu he built Chenghua Hall, twice as high as Chengguang; corvée at the north gate made earth as costly as grain.

sentences.zh: 典軍杜靜載棺詣闕，上書極諫。

translations.literal: The Director of the Army Du Jing carried a coffin to the gate and memorialized with utmost remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The director of the army Du Jing brought a coffin to the gate and memorialized in strongest protest.

sentences.zh: 熙大怒，斬之。

translations.literal: Xi was greatly angry and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi in fury beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 苻氏嘗季夏思凍魚膾，仲冬須生地黃，皆下有司切責，不得，加以大辟，其虐也如此。

translations.literal: The Fu clan once in the height of summer longed for frozen fish sliced thin, and in mid-winter required fresh rehmannia from the field—both were ordered from the offices with stern demand; when they could not obtain them, the death penalty was added—such was their cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fu once craved frozen fish in midsummer and fresh rehmannia in midwinter; the offices were driven with threats and failure brought death—such was their cruelty.

sentences.zh: 苻氏死，熙悲號躃踴，若喪考妣，擁其屍而撫之曰：「體已就冷，命遂斷矣！

translations.literal: When the Fu clan died, Xi wailed and stamped in grief as if he had lost father and mother; embracing her corpse he stroked it and said: "The body is already cold, life is cut off!"
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Fu died, Xi wailed and stamped as for father and mother, embraced her corpse and cried: "The body is cold, life is ended!"

sentences.zh: 」於是僵僕氣絕，久而乃蘇。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stiffened and fell, breath cut off, and only after long did he revive.
translations.idiomatic: He stiffened and ceased breathing, reviving only after long moments.

sentences.zh: 大斂既訖，復啟其棺而與交接。

translations.literal: When the great encoffining was finished, he again opened the coffin and joined with her in intercourse.
translations.idiomatic: After the great encoffining he opened the coffin again and lay with her corpse.

sentences.zh: 服斬縗，食粥。

translations.literal: He wore the hemp of deepest mourning and ate gruel.
translations.idiomatic: He wore deepest mourning hemp and ate only gruel.

sentences.zh: 制百僚于宮內哭臨，令沙門素服。

translations.literal: He ordered the hundred officials to mourn within the palace; he ordered Buddhist monks to wear white robes.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the hundred officials to mourn within the palace and monks to wear white.

sentences.zh: 使有司案檢哭者，有淚以為忠孝，無則罪之，於是群臣震懼，莫不含辛以為淚焉。

translations.literal: He had the offices investigate those who mourned: those with tears were deemed loyal and filial, those without were punished; the ministers all trembled in fear and none failed to squeeze out bitter tears.
translations.idiomatic: He had mourners inspected: tears meant loyalty, dryness meant guilt; the ministers trembled and squeezed out bitter tears.

sentences.zh: 慕容隆妻張氏，熙之嫂也，美姿容，有巧思。

translations.literal: Murong Long's wife, Lady Zhang, was Xi's sister-in-law, beautiful in appearance and clever in craft.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Long's wife Lady Zhang, Xi's sister-in-law, was beautiful and clever.

sentences.zh: 熙將以為苻氏之殉，欲以罪殺之，乃毀其禭靴，中有弊氈，遂賜死。

translations.literal: Xi was about to make her follow the Fu clan in burial; wishing to kill her on a charge, he ruined her burial boots—in them were worn felts—and thereupon gave her death.
translations.idiomatic: Xi meant to bury her with Lady Fu; to kill her on a charge he ruined her burial boots—worn felts were found inside—and sentenced her to death.

sentences.zh: 三女叩頭求哀，熙不許。

translations.literal: Her three daughters knocked their heads begging mercy; Xi would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Her three daughters begged on their knees; Xi refused.

sentences.zh: 制公卿已下至於百姓，率戶營墓，費殫府藏。

translations.literal: He ordered from the highest dukes and ministers down to the common people that each household should build a tomb, exhausting the treasury stores.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every household from dukes to commoners to build tombs, exhausting the treasury.

sentences.zh: 下錮三泉，周輸數里，內則圖畫尚書八坐之象。

translations.literal: Below he set triple springs, encircling several li; within were painted the images of the eight seats of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Below he set triple springs encircling several li, painted within with the eight seats of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 熙曰：「善為之，朕將隨後入此陵。

translations.literal: Xi said: "Do it well—I shall follow afterward into this mausoleum."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said: "Do it well—I shall follow into this tomb afterward."

sentences.zh: 」識者以為不祥。

translations.literal: Those who understood held it inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The knowing called it ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 其右僕射韋璆等並懼為殉，沐浴而待死焉。

translations.literal: His Right Vice Minister of Works Wei Qiu and the others all feared they would be buried alive and bathed awaiting death.
translations.idiomatic: His right vice minister Wei Qiu and others feared living burial and bathed awaiting death.

sentences.zh: 號苻氏墓曰征平陵。

translations.literal: He styled the Fu clan's tomb Zhengping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He named Lady Fu's tomb Zhengping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 熙被髮徒跣，步從苻氏喪。

translations.literal: Xi with loose hair and bare feet walked following the Fu clan's funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Xi with hair loose and feet bare walked in Lady Fu's funeral train.

sentences.zh: 轜車高大，毀北門而出。

translations.literal: The bier carriage was tall and large; they destroyed the northern gate to take it out.
translations.idiomatic: The bier carriage was so tall they destroyed the north gate to pass it out.

sentences.zh: 長老竊相謂曰：「慕容氏自毀其門，將不久也。」

translations.literal: The elders whispered to one another: "The Murong clan destroys its own gate—they will not last long."
translations.idiomatic: The elders whispered: "The Murong destroy their own gate—they will not last."

sentences.zh: 中衛將軍馮跋、左衛將軍張興，先皆坐事亡奔，以熙政之虐也，與跋從兄萬泥等二十二人結盟，推慕容雲為主，發尚方徒五千餘人閉門距守。

translations.literal: The Central Guard General Feng Ba and the Left Guard General Zhang Xing, both earlier having sat in crimes and fled, because Xi's government was cruel formed a covenant with Ba's cousin Wan Ni and twenty-two others, pushed Murong Yun as leader, and raised more than five thousand convict laborers of the Imperial Workshop to shut the gates and resist.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba, central guard general, and Zhang Xing, left guard general, both fugitives from earlier crimes, because Xi's rule was cruel allied with Ba's cousin Wan Ni and twenty-two others, made Murong Yun their leader, and shut the gates with five thousand convict laborers.

sentences.zh: 中黃門趙洛生奔告之，熙曰：「此鼠盜耳，朕還當誅之。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant Zhao Luosheng fled to report it; Xi said: "These are rat bandits—I shall return and execute them."
translations.idiomatic: The palace attendant Zhao Luosheng fled to report; Xi said: "Rat thieves—I shall return and kill them."

sentences.zh: 」乃收發貫甲，馳還赴難。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gathered armor and galloped back to answer the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered armor and galloped back.

sentences.zh: 夜至龍城，攻北門不克，遂敗，走入龍騰宛，微服隱于林中，為人所執，雲得而弑之，及其諸子同殯城北。

translations.literal: By night he reached Longcheng, attacked the northern gate without success, was defeated, fled into Longteng Garden, went in disguise into the woods, was seized by men; Yun obtained him and assassinated him, and with his sons was buried together north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: By night he reached Longcheng, failed at the north gate, fled into Longteng Garden, hid in the woods in disguise, was seized; Yun killed him and buried him with his sons north of the city.

sentences.zh: 時年二十三，在位六年。

translations.literal: He was twenty-three years old and had reigned six years.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-three and had reigned six years.

sentences.zh: 雲葬之於苻氏墓，偽諡昭文皇帝。

translations.literal: Yun buried him at the Fu clan's tomb and gave the posthumous title Emperor Zhaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Yun buried him at Lady Fu's tomb and posthumously titled him Emperor Zhaowen.

sentences.zh: 垂以孝武帝太元八年僭立，至熙四世，凡二十四年，以安帝義熙三年滅。

translations.literal: Chui usurped the throne in the eighth year of Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan era; to Xi was four generations, altogether twenty-four years; it perished in the third year of Emperor An's Yixi era.
translations.idiomatic: Chui usurped rule in the eighth year of Taiyuan; through four generations to Xi was twenty-four years; the state perished in the third year of Yixi.

sentences.zh: 初，童謠曰：「一束槁，兩頭然，禿頭小兒來滅燕。

translations.literal: Earlier a children's song said: "A bundle of straw, burning at both ends, a bald-headed boy comes to destroy Yan."
translations.idiomatic: A children's song had said: "A bundle of straw burning at both ends—a bald-headed boy comes to destroy Yan."

sentences.zh: 」槁字上有草，下有禾，兩頭然則禾草俱盡而成高字。

translations.literal: The character for straw has grass above and grain below; burning at both ends means grain and grass are both exhausted and form the character Gao.
translations.idiomatic: The character for straw has grass above and grain below; burning both ends leaves the character Gao.

sentences.zh: 雲父名拔，小字禿頭，三子，而雲季也。

translations.literal: Yun's father's name was Ba, childhood name Bald Head; of three sons Yun was the youngest.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's father was named Ba, childhood name Bald Head; of three sons Yun was the youngest.

sentences.zh: 熙竟為雲所滅，如謠言焉。

translations.literal: Xi in the end was destroyed by Yun, as the song said.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was destroyed by Yun, as the song foretold.

sentences.zh: 慕容雲，字子雨，寶之養子也。

translations.literal: Murong Yun, styled Ziyu, was Bao's adopted son.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yun, whose courtesy name was Ziyu, was Bao's adopted son.

sentences.zh: 祖父和，高句驪之支庶，自雲高陽氏之苗裔，故以高為氏焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather He was a collateral branch of Koguryo; Yun himself claimed descent from the Gaoyang clan, and therefore took Gao as surname.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather He was a collateral line of Koguryo; Yun claimed descent from Gaoyang and took Gao as surname.

sentences.zh: 雲沈深有局量，厚重希言，時人咸以為愚，唯馮跋奇其志度而友之。

translations.literal: Yun was deep and reserved with capacity and measure, heavy and sparing of words; men of the time all thought him foolish—only Feng Ba marveled at his ambition and bearing and befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was deep, reserved, and sparing of speech; the world thought him a fool—only Feng Ba saw his ambition and befriended him.

sentences.zh: 寶之為太子，雲以武藝給事侍東宮，拜侍御郎，襲敗慕容會軍。

translations.literal: When Bao was crown prince, Yun with martial arts served in attendance at the Eastern Palace, was appointed Attendant Lang, and defeated Murong Hui's army.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao was crown prince, Yun served the Eastern Palace with martial skill, was made attendant, and defeated Murong Hui's army.

sentences.zh: 寶子之，賜姓慕容氏，封夕陽公。

translations.literal: Bao made him his son, bestowed the surname Murong, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Bao adopted him, gave him the surname Murong, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 熙之葬苻氏也，馮跋詣雲，告之以謀。

translations.literal: When Xi buried the Fu clan, Feng Ba went to Yun and told him the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi buried Lady Fu, Feng Ba came to Yun with the plot.

sentences.zh: 雲懼曰：「吾嬰疾歷年，卿等所知，願更圖之。

translations.literal: Yun in fear said: "I have suffered illness for years—you all know this; I wish you would make another plan."
translations.idiomatic: Yun in fear said: "I have been ill for years, as you know; choose another leader."

sentences.zh: 」跋逼曰：「慕容氏世衰，河間虐暴，惑妖淫之女而逆亂天常，百姓不堪其害，思亂者十室九焉，此天亡之時也。

translations.literal: Ba pressed him: "The Murong clan declines generation by generation; the Prince of Hejian is cruel and violent, deluded by a demonic woman and perverting heaven's constants—the common people cannot bear their harm, and those who think of rebellion are nine out of ten households; this is the time heaven destroys them."
translations.idiomatic: Ba pressed him: "The Murong decline; Xi is cruel, ruled by a witch, and perverts heaven's law—the people cannot bear it and nine in ten wish rebellion. Heaven destroys them now."

sentences.zh: 公自高氏名家，何能為他養子！

translations.literal: "You yourself are of a famous house of the Gao clan—how can you be another's adopted son!"
translations.idiomatic: "You are of the noble house of Gao—how remain another's adopted son!"

sentences.zh: 機運難邀，千歲一時，公焉得辭也！

translations.literal: "Opportunity is hard to invite, a thousand years has one such moment—how can you decline!"
translations.idiomatic: "Fortune comes once in a thousand years—how can you refuse!"

sentences.zh: 」扶之而出。

translations.literal: They supported him and led him out.
translations.idiomatic: They raised him and led him out.

sentences.zh: 雲曰：「吾疾苦日久，廢絕世務。

translations.literal: Yun said: "My illness and suffering have been long; I have abandoned worldly affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said: "My illness is long; I have left the world behind."

sentences.zh: 卿今興建大事，謬見推逼。

translations.literal: "You now raise a great affair and wrongly push me forward."
translations.idiomatic: "You raise a great affair and wrongly force me forward."

sentences.zh: 所以徘徊，非為身也，實惟否德不足以濟元元故耳。

translations.literal: "The reason I hesitate is not for my person—it is truly that my virtue is not sufficient to aid the masses."
translations.idiomatic: "I hesitate not for myself but because my virtue cannot save the people."

sentences.zh: 」跋等強之，雲遂即天王位，復姓高氏，大赦境內殊死以下，改元曰正始，國號大燕。

translations.literal: Ba and the others forced him; Yun thereupon assumed the title of Heavenly King, resumed the surname Gao, proclaimed a general amnesty short of death within the borders, changed the era name to Zhengshi, and the state name to Great Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Ba and the others forced him; Yun took the title Heavenly King, resumed the surname Gao, amnestied the realm, proclaimed the Zhengshi era, and named the state Great Yan.

sentences.zh: 署馮跋侍中、都督中外諸軍事、征北大將軍、開府儀同三司、錄尚書事、武邑公，封伯、子、男，鄉、亭侯者五十餘人，士卒賜穀帛有差。

translations.literal: He appointed Feng Ba Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, Northern Expedition Grand General, Commissioner with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Wuyi; he enfeoffed more than fifty as marquises, earls, viscounts, barons, and village and precinct marquises; soldiers received grain and silk each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He made Feng Ba attendant-in-ordinary, commander-in-chief, northern expedition grand general, commissioner equal to the three excellencies, director of the masters of writing, and duke of Wuyi; enfeoffed more than fifty marquises and earls; soldiers received grain and silk by rank.

sentences.zh: 熙之群官，復其爵位。

translations.literal: Xi's host of officials—all had their ranks and fiefs restored.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's officials all had rank and fief restored.

sentences.zh: 立妻李氏為天王後，子彭為太子。

translations.literal: He installed his wife Lady Li as Heavenly Queen and his son Peng as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He made his wife Lady Li heavenly queen and his son Peng crown prince.

sentences.zh: 越騎校尉慕輿良謀叛，雲誅之。

translations.literal: The Rapid Cavalry Commandant Murong Liang plotted rebellion; Yun executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The rapid cavalry commandant Murong Liang plotted rebellion; Yun executed him.

sentences.zh: 雲臨東堂，幸臣離班、桃仁懷劍執紙而入，稱有所啟，拔劍擊雲，雲以幾距班，桃仁進而弑之。

translations.literal: Yun faced the Eastern Hall; his favored minister Li Ban and Taoren, carrying swords, entered holding paper, claiming they had something to report; they drew swords and struck Yun; Yun used a table to block Ban; Taoren advanced and assassinated him.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Hall, favored ministers Li Ban and Taoren entered with swords claiming to report, struck Yun—he blocked Ban with a table—and Taoren advanced and killed him.

sentences.zh: 馮跋遷雲屍於東宮，偽諡惠懿皇帝。

translations.literal: Feng Ba moved Yun's corpse to the Eastern Palace and gave the posthumous title Emperor Huiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba moved Yun's body to the Eastern Palace and posthumously titled him Emperor Huiyi.

sentences.zh: 雲自以無功德而為豪桀所推，常內懷懼，故寵養壯士以為腹心。

translations.literal: Yun, because he had no merit yet was pushed by the bold, always harbored fear within; therefore he favored and nourished stalwarts as his heart and bowels.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, having no merit yet pushed forward by bold men, lived in inner fear and so favored stalwarts as his claws and teeth.

sentences.zh: 離班、桃仁等並專典禁衛，委之以爪牙之任，賞賜月至數千萬，衣食臥起皆與之同，終以此致敗雲。

translations.literal: Li Ban, Taoren, and the others all exclusively held the palace guard; he entrusted them with the task of claw and fang, bestowing tens of millions monthly in rewards; in food, clothing, lying down and rising he was the same with them—in the end through this he was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ban, Taoren, and others held the palace guard exclusively; he gave them tens of millions monthly, shared food and bed with them—and through this was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：四星東聚，金陵之氣已分；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: When the four stars gathered in the east, the breath of Jinling was already divided;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When the four stars gathered in the east, Jinling's fate was already divided;

sentences.zh: 五馬南浮，玉塞之雄方擾。

translations.literal: when the five horses floated south, the heroes of the jade frontier were just in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: when the five horses floated south, the frontier heroes were in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 市朝屢改，艱虞靡息。

translations.literal: Markets and courts changed repeatedly; hardship and peril never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Markets and courts shifted endlessly; hardship never ceased.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂天資英傑，威震本朝，以雄略見猜而庇身寬政，永固受之而以禮，道明事之而畢力。

translations.literal: Murong Chui by nature's gift was an heroic outstanding man, awe-inspiring in his own court; because his bold strategy was suspected he sheltered himself in lenient government; Yonggu accepted him with ritual, Daoming served affairs and exhausted his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui was a natural hero, awe-inspiring at home; suspected for his bold strategy he sheltered under lenient rule; Fu Jian received him with ritual, and he served with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 然而隼質難羈，狼心自野。

translations.literal: Yet falcon nature is hard to bind, wolf heart is wild by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Yet falcon nature cannot be bound, wolf heart runs wild.

sentences.zh: 淮南失律，三甥之謀已構；

translations.literal: Huainan lost discipline—the plot of the three nephews was already formed;
translations.idiomatic: Huainan lost order—the three nephews' plot was formed;

sentences.zh: 河朔分麾，五木之祥雲啟。

translations.literal: north of the Yellow River banners divided—the auspicious clouds of the Five Mu opened.
translations.idiomatic: north of the Yellow River banners divided—the omen of the Five Mu opened.

sentences.zh: 斬飛龍而遐舉，逾石門而長邁，遂使翟氏景從，鄴師宵逸，收羅趙、魏，驅駕英雄。

translations.literal: He cut down the flying dragon and soared afar, crossed Shimen and marched long—thereupon the Di clan followed in prospect, Ye's armies fled by night; he gathered Zhao and Wei, drove and harnessed heroes.
translations.idiomatic: He struck down the flying dragon and soared away, crossed Shimen and marched far—Di clans followed, Ye's armies fled by night; he gathered Zhao and Wei and drove heroes before him.

sentences.zh: 叩囊餘奇，摧五萬于河曲；

translations.literal: Tapping the bag's remaining marvels, he crushed fifty thousand at the river bend;
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on hidden stratagems, he crushed fifty thousand at the river bend;

sentences.zh: 浮船秘策，招七郡于黎陽。

translations.literal: with secret plans on floating boats he recruited seven commanderies at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: with secret plans on floating boats he won seven commanderies at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 返遼陰之舊物，創中山之新社，類帝禋宗，僭擬斯備。

translations.literal: He recovered the old things of Liaoyin, founded the new community of Zhongshan; imitating the Emperor in sacrifice to the ancestors, usurpation was complete.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Liaoyin's old lands, founded Zhongshan's new state; mimicking imperial rites, usurpation was complete.

sentences.zh: 夫以重耳歸晉，賴五臣之功；

translations.literal: How can there be achievement different from the two hegemons, masses slight and hosts a single brigade, prying and pulling to topple mountains and peaks, soaring and roaring to ride wind and clouds!
translations.idiomatic: How could one brigade pry down mountains and ride wind and clouds—yet he did, though unlike the two hegemons in scale!

sentences.zh: 句踐紿吳，資五千之卒。

translations.literal: Though Wey forgot extinction and passed it on in the eastern state, and Duke Mu of Qin had surplus yet was shamed before the western neighbor—truly Fu Jian's treacherous ways were not Jin's whale and kraken.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wey forgot extinction in the east and Duke Mu of Qin was shamed in the west—Fu Jian's treachery was not Jin's whale.

sentences.zh: 惡有業殊二霸，眾微一旅，掎拔而傾山嶽，騰嘯而禦風雲！

translations.literal: Bao by floating reputation obtained advancement, with harsh texts controlled the age; within the inner quarters resentment flared, fierce enemies pressed from without—though poison did not reach things, enough evil destroyed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Bao rose on empty reputation, ruled with harsh law; inner court seethed, fierce enemies pressed without—his poison turned on himself.

sentences.zh: 雖衛人忘亡復傳于東國，任好余裕伊愧於西鄰，信苻氏之奸回，非晉室之鯨鯢矣。

translations.literal: Sheng then had filial brotherhood in hidden accord, civil and martial not fallen; he hid his light and pacified enemy and bandit, blamed himself and yielded high peril—gracefully the fine captive of a turbid age.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng matched filial brotherhood in secret, civil and martial unbroken; he hid his light, pacified foes, blamed himself and yielded peril—a graceful captive of a turbid age.

sentences.zh: 寶以浮譽獲升，峻文禦俗，蕭牆內憤，勍敵外陵，雖毒不被物而惡足自剿。

translations.literal: Xi then was not the hidden lord of the land; his rise entirely through dissolute virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was no hidden lord of the land; he rose entirely through lust.

sentences.zh: 盛則孝友冥符，文武不墜，韜光而夷仇賊，罪己而遜高危，翩翩然濁世之佳虜矣。

translations.literal: The manner of Li Rong pleased on the couch;
translations.idiomatic: Li Rong's manner pleased on the couch;

sentences.zh: 熙乃地非奧主，舉因淫德。

translations.literal: the beauty of Xuan Qi was marvelled at in black hair.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Qi's beauty was marvelled at in her black hair.

sentences.zh: 驪戎之態，取悅于匡床；

translations.literal: He floated light boats on the sea of Quguang, gazed on morning ford at Jingyun Mountain, adorned earth and wood to feed arrogant heart, exhausted lamentation in the smallest soil—ancestral sacrifices were destroyed, and he became what the Feng clan drove away.
translations.idiomatic: He floated on Quguang's sea, gazed from Jingyun's heights, adorned earth and wood to feed pride, exhausted the realm in lament—ancestral rites perished, and the Feng clan drove him away.

sentences.zh: 玄妻之姿，見奇於鬒發。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: The barbarians relied on force, mountains and rivers seethed.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Barbarians relied on force; mountains and rivers seethed.

sentences.zh: 蕩輕舟于曲光之海，望朝涉于景雲之山，飾土木於驕心，窮怨嗟於蕞壤，宗祀夷滅，為馮氏之驅除焉。

translations.literal: Heaven had not yet repented of calamity; men were not those who could.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven had not yet repented; men were not equal to the task.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：戎狄憑陵，山川沸騰。

translations.literal: Swift running and keen striking—who calls first, rises.
translations.idiomatic: Swift running, keen striking—who calls first, rises.

sentences.zh: 天未悔禍，人非與能。

translations.literal: Daoming blazing bright, whipping the bold and heroic.
translations.idiomatic: Daoming blazing bright, whipping heroes.

sentences.zh: 疾走而捷，先鳴則興。

translations.literal: Swift running and keen striking—who calls first, rises.
translations.idiomatic: Swift running, keen striking—who calls first, rises.

sentences.zh: 道明烈烈，鞭笞豪傑。

translations.literal: Daoming blazing bright, whipping the bold and heroic.
translations.idiomatic: Daoming blazing bright, whipping heroes.

sentences.zh: 掃燕夷魏，釗屠永滅。

translations.literal: He swept Yan, pacified Wei, cut down and slaughtered forever extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He swept Yan, pacified Wei, cut down foes forever.

sentences.zh: 大盜潛移，鴻名遂竊。

translations.literal: The great robber secretly shifted; the great name was stolen.
translations.idiomatic: The great robber shifted in secret; the great name was stolen.

sentences.zh: 寶心生亂，盛清家難。

translations.literal: Bao's heart bred disorder; Sheng cleared family hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's heart bred disorder; Sheng cleared family hardship.

sentences.zh: 熙極驕淫，人懷憤惋。

translations.literal: Xi reached utmost pride and dissipation; men harbored indignant regret.
translations.idiomatic: Xi reached utmost pride and lust; men nursed indignant rage.

sentences.zh: 孽貽身咎，災無以逭。

translations.literal: Crime bequeathed body-trouble; calamity could not be escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Sin brought bodily ruin; calamity could not be escaped.
